Title: KLIA security: someone, somewhere is failing to do their job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: There used to be a time when you could arrive at the airport just minutes before a flight and breeze through a relatively hassle-free process of boarding a plane.
You checked in, walked towards the gate and, barring the occasional random check, got on with your journey. Airport security meant little more than a quick pat-down by personnel armed with hand-held metal detector wands.
Nobody asked you to remove your shoes, belt, watch, bangle, jacket, coat, hat, bandana or whatever else airport security happened to take an interest in that particular day.
Those days are long gone.
Today, you can attract suspicion simply by absent-mindedly leaving your laptop or other electronic devices inside your luggage instead of placing them in a separate tray for scanning.
Then comes the inevitable interrogation from the bored-looking X-ray scanning officer about that slightly thicker-than-usual tube of toothpaste in your cabin baggage.
God forbid you forgot about that bottle of Spritzer. The stares and sudden frenetic activity... you may as well have been carrying the binary component of a VX nerve agent.
And the more you hurry through security, the more likely you are to discover some mysterious metal object in your pocket just as you walk through the detector.
All these enhanced measures were introduced in the name of making air travel safer following the 9/11 terrorist attacks and subsequent plots involving, among others, the failed shoe bomber, the terrorist who attempted to detonate liquid explosives aboard an airliner and the nutcase who tried to set off an improvised explosive device hidden in his underwear.
These incidents triggered a sweeping overhaul of airport security worldwide — shoes had to come off, liquids, gels and aerosols were restricted from carry-on luggage, full-body scanners using advanced imaging technology were installed, and bomb-sniffing dogs were brought in to bolster airport security.
All of this is now familiar at our very own Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Yet somehow, smugglers have still managed to get some rather remarkable things past the layers of security, including:
— live gibbons, marbled polecats, lutung and palm civets stuffed into suitcases,
— live snakes hidden in clothing,
— turtles taped to people's bodies, and
— baby crocodiles packed into checked baggage.
Most of this wildlife was smuggled aboard flights leaving KLIA, only to be discovered at foreign airports.
It is no secret that trafficking syndicates continue to exploit enforcement loopholes and weaknesses at KLIA. What is baffling is how they can do so despite the layers of security supposedly designed to stop them.
How does an entire suitcase packed with live animals evade detection at KLIA?
It is a question made even more difficult to answer when sniffer dogs are also deployed at the airport to assist in enforcement.
Now KLIA's security reputation has taken another hit following the recent arrest in Jakarta of a pilot caught carrying 26kg of ecstasy pills out of KLIA.
That incident should set off alarm bells.
[[nid:1508498]]
It raises serious questions about whether existing security protocols are capable of detecting and preventing not only drug trafficking, but threats that could have far more catastrophic consequences for aviation safety and passenger lives.
As expected, the authorities were quick to respond, announcing plans to beef up security and screening protocols at airports, with greater emphasis on drugs and contraband.
Shockingly, the Home Ministry also admitted that screening protocols had, until then, prioritised weapons detection over other threats.
Not surprisingly, the announcement that existing scanners would also be reviewed for possible upgrades followed soon after.
But one need not be an Einstein to figure out that 26kg of drugs did not simply "sail through" KLIA scanners because the officers operating them were looking for firearms rather than drugs.
If that were the case, how do we explain the water bottles, nail clippers, oversized tubes of toothpaste and expensive perfume bottles that are routinely seized at the first security checkpoints?
The issue cannot simply be the scanners.
More troubling is the lack of updates on investigations into how the wildlife and drugs were able to get through KLIA in the first place.
It requires a suspension of disbelief to accept that suitcases filled with live animals or large quantities of drugs could repeatedly make it through multiple layers of security without someone, somewhere, failing to do their job — or worse, helping them get through.
What is obvious is that there is nothing wrong with the security systems at KLIA. What needs to go under the microscope is the enforcement — the procedures, the supervision and, most importantly, the people manning the country's main gateway in and out.
If we are serious about tackling smuggling out of KLIA, those responsible for airport security must be held accountable every time smugglers and traffickers are caught with items that left the airport undetected and were only discovered after reaching foreign destinations.
There must be answers as to how suitcases filled with drugs and protected wildlife can pass through layer after layer of security, only to be discovered thousands of kilometres away.
The bigger question is whether anyone is prepared to look beyond the machines and examine the people behind them.
KLIA should not be a place where a forgotten bottle of water is treated as a security threat while 26kg of ecstasy can somehow make it out of the country.
Because when contraband repeatedly slips through the front door, the problem may not be that we need a bigger lock.
Maybe we need to find out who keeps leaving the door open.
* The writer is New Straits Times deputy group editor

Title: Sime Darby's growth engine shifts into higher gear
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A stronger core, leaner balance sheet and regional diversification are giving Sime Darby Bhd room to navigate intensifying competition and global uncertainty.
As a Malaysian multinational corporation, Sime Darby is betting that the strength of its core businesses - rather than a fresh wave of acquisitions - will drive its next phase of growth as it navigates a more volatile regional economy.
The strategy is already gaining traction.
For the nine months ended March 31, 2026, Sime Darby's net profit rose 10.9 per cent to RM1.44 billion, while revenue edged up to RM52.8 billion from RM52.3 billion a year earlier.
Core net profit for the third quarter jumped 55.6 per cent to RM263 million, excluding a one-off RM434 million gain from the disposal of Malaysia Vision Valley land, with all three core businesses delivering stronger profits.
For group chief executive officer Datuk Jeffri Salim Davidson, the latest results are not just a short-term upswing.
It is also the outcome of a deliberate strategy centred on focusing the group on automotive and industrial equipment across Asia Pacific.
"These results reflect the strategy we have been executing over the past several years, focusing on our core automotive and industrial equipment trading businesses across Asia Pacific," he told Business Times.
"Our international footprint allows us to capture growth opportunities across key markets, while providing resilience through diversification and helping us balance cyclical trends within the portfolio."
Motors Take The Lead
The automotive business has emerged as an important growth engine, benefiting from stronger vehicle sales in Singapore and China, and higher assembly revenue in Malaysia.
Sime Darby's broad portfolio also gives it exposure to different segments of a rapidly changing automotive market, from mass-market vehicles to premium brands and fast-growing EVs.
In Singapore, BYD has emerged as the top-selling automotive brand, while BMW is the leading premium EV marque.
Malaysia, meanwhile, recorded higher vehicle sales in the first half of FY2026, supported by stronger passenger vehicle demand, rising EV adoption and promotional activity.
The Malaysian Automotive Association has raised its 2026 total industry volume forecast to 800,000 units from 790,000 previously.
Jeffri said Sime Darby's strategy is to participate across the automotive spectrum while using its scale, partnerships and aftersales capabilities to remain competitive.
"The automotive industry is undergoing a structural shift with the acceleration of EV adoption and the growing presence of new entrants," he said.
The acquisition of UMW Holdings Bhd has also strengthened Sime Darby's automotive earnings base.
Perodua achieved record sales in 2025, while Toyota has sold more than 100,000 vehicles annually for four consecutive years.
Both brands continue to benefit from established reputations, extensive dealer and aftersales networks, deep localisation and strong vendor ecosystems despite rising competition from Chinese manufacturers.
"The acquisition of UMW was clearly the right move and continues to contribute positively to the group's overall performance," Jeffri said.
Sime Darby manages the various brands under its portfolio independently with separate professional teams, allowing Toyota, Perodua, BYD and Hyundai to serve different market segments.
China A Test Of Staying Power
China, however, remains the more challenging part of the automotive equation.
Heavy discounting and intense competition from domestic Chinese brands continue to pressure the market, although Sime Darby has seen some improvement in its BMW business following dealer support measures and rebates from the manufacturer.
The group remains committed to BMW in China and expects the arrival of BMW's Neue Klasse range in the fourth quarter of 2026 to provide a potential boost to sales.
"We remain committed to BMW in China," the CEO said, noting that Sime Darby remains among the marque's top-performing dealers in the country.
The group is nevertheless managing the business cautiously through cost optimisation and tighter inventory management.
At the same time, Sime Darby has streamlined its portfolio by divesting underperforming businesses, particularly non-core operations where returns did not meet expectations.
Less Debt, More Firepower
The group's ability to weather these pressures has been strengthened by progress on its balance sheet.
Following the UMW acquisition, Sime Darby's gearing rose as expected. But improved operating cash flow and disciplined working capital management have since helped bring debt down.
The result was a reduction of more than RM100 million in finance costs during the first nine months of 2026.
Jeffri said the group's priority now is to preserve financial flexibility and reinvest in its existing businesses rather than chase major acquisitions. "We will continue to strengthen our balance sheet and maintain financial flexibility."
That approach gives Sime Darby greater resilience as global energy disruptions and higher input costs create fresh uncertainties.
Industrial Bets Beyond The Cycle
The group's industrial division is facing softer product support and rental activity as some mining customers defer maintenance spending to conserve cash.
But Sime Darby remains bullish on the long-term prospects of Australasia, where it has significant exposure to Australia's resources sector.
The group sees particular opportunity in commodities such as copper, which is increasingly important to the global EV and renewable-energy transition.
Its acquisition of Onsite in South Australia has also broadened its exposure to battery and critical minerals, including copper and uranium.
Jeffri said the group remains confident despite current caution among some mining customers, as commodity demand remains supportive and activity is expected to normalise.
Regional Scale As A Buffer
For Sime Darby, diversification is not simply about having operations in multiple countries.
The group operates in 18 countries and territories across Asia Pacific and participates across the value chain - from distribution and retail to assembly, product support and aftersales.
That regional reach allows it to balance cyclical swings between markets while strengthening relationships with global principals.
"Our international footprint is a key strength, but it is very much anchored in a focused strategy," Jeffri said.
The group is also using its regional operations to develop Malaysian talent, giving employees international exposure while bringing global best practices back into the domestic market.
Focus, Not Expansion For Expansion's Sake
The underlying message from Sime Darby's latest performance is one of consolidation rather than aggressive expansion.
After years of reshaping its portfolio and completing the transformational UMW acquisition, the group is now focused on extracting greater value from the businesses it already owns.
Its next phase looks to be shaped by three priorities: growing automotive earnings, riding the long-term resources cycle and maintaining financial discipline.
"We take a long-term view while remaining prepared for the recovery in demand," Jeffri said of the industrial business.
For a group operating across markets exposed to very different economic cycles, that patience may prove as important as its scale.

Title: No Middle East data centre windfall, but Malaysia eyes next wave
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is unlikely to inherit a windfall of data centre investments from the Middle East despite rising geopolitical tensions, but the turmoil could strengthen its hand in the race for the next wave of global digital infrastructure spending.
Industry experts said billions of dollars in projects already committed in the Middle East are unlikely to be uprooted, particularly those backed by sovereign wealth funds and tied to national artificial intelligence (AI) and economic ambitions.
Instead, Malaysia – and Johor in particular – could emerge as a stronger destination for fresh investments as global technology companies increasingly spread their bets across different markets to reduce geographic risk.
The stakes are significant. The Middle East has 2.2 gigawatts (GW) of data centre capacity under construction, more than double its existing operational capacity of 1GW, with another 12GW planned, according to JLL's EMEA Year-End Data Centre Report 2025.
Recent geopolitical developments have raised questions over whether some of that investment could find its way to lower-risk destinations such as Malaysia.
COMMITTED CAPITAL UNLIKELY TO MOVE
But economist Geoffrey Williams said data centres are long-term investments and geopolitical risks would typically have been weighed long before capital was committed.
"Data centres are long-term investments. The geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are long-term issues. So investors have taken all the risks into account but are still planning significant investments in the Middle East," he said.
Williams said investors choosing the Middle East would also likely have evaluated alternative destinations, including Malaysia, before proceeding with their projects.
As such, he said a substantial diversion of existing investments into Southeast Asia or Malaysia was unlikely if these markets were not already part of investors' expansion plans.
JLL Malaysia capital markets and data centre director Keith Eng shared a similar view, saying most projects currently underway in the Middle East are backed by sovereign wealth and national development strategies.
"These projects are designed to serve local markets and are unlikely to relocate," he told Business Times.
Eng said many developments are closely linked to national AI ambitions and data sovereignty requirements, effectively anchoring the investments to their home markets.
"Projects like Saudi Arabia's NEOM, a 1.5GW renewable-powered campus, are geographically anchored and tied to national economic transformation strategies. Direct redirection of these committed projects is therefore unlikely," he said.
JOHOR EYES THE NEXT WAVE
The bigger opportunity for Malaysia, Eng said, is not in poaching projects from the Middle East but capturing additional investments as operators seek greater geographic diversification amid an increasingly uncertain global environment.
"Malaysia's fundamentals make it a natural choice for incremental investment rather than a substitute location," he said.
Johor is well positioned to capture future growth, backed by its strategic location, land availability, expanding power infrastructure, extensive submarine cable connectivity and stable regulatory environment, Eng said.
The state is already undergoing a rapid build-out.
"The market's capacity will double from 850MW at end-2025 to approximately 2,000MW by end-2026, with an additional 2.7GW in the pipeline and planned for completion over the next three to five years," he said.
Johor has emerged as one of Asia-Pacific's fastest-growing data centre markets, benefiting from its proximity to Singapore, where constraints on new developments have pushed operators to look beyond the city-state for expansion.
POWER, WATER COULD TEST GROWTH
However, Malaysia may not have unlimited room to take on another surge in investment.
Both experts cautioned that infrastructure constraints, particularly electricity and water supply, could limit how quickly Johor can accommodate additional projects.
Williams said Johor's current capacity planning is based on projected long-term demand and would not be able to immediately absorb a significant diversion of investment.
"Any surge in new data centre investments would cause a significant strain on electricity and water resources which are already under review from current plans," he said.
Eng likewise identified power infrastructure as the most immediate challenge, warning that the rapid pace of development could create bottlenecks if grid expansion fails to keep pace.
Still, he said Malaysia remains well placed to benefit from a broader shift among hyperscalers and cloud providers towards spreading investments across multiple regions.
Rather than triggering a wholesale migration of Middle Eastern data centre projects to Southeast Asia, geopolitical uncertainty could therefore make diversification increasingly important in future investment decisions.
For Malaysia, the prize may not be capital fleeing the Middle East, but the next dollar that global technology companies decide to deploy elsewhere.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump insists Netanyahu relationship 'very good' despite Gaza rift
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump insisted Monday that his relationship with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is "very good" despite the Israeli leader's rejection of a US-led Gaza plan.
"The relationship is very good," Trump said in response to a shouted question from a journalist at the end of an Oval Office event.
After more than a week of gradually escalating criticism, Netanyahu explicitly stated on Sunday that he opposed the Gaza plan, which called for Israel to begin pulling back forces in tandem with disarmament by Hamas.
Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, is running even or trailing in some polls ahead of October 27 elections, the country's first since the devastating 2023 attack by Hamas that sparked the Gaza war.
Polls show that the Gaza plan is unpopular with Netanyahu's right-wing base, and far-right members of his cabinet had urged him to kill it.

Title: Special Dewan sitting today to deliberate Tabung Haji RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat is set to convene a special meeting today to discuss and deliberate on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report regarding Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
The one-day session, which begins at 10am, will be broadcast live on the Parliament's YouTube platform and official media channels.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan will begin the proceedings with an explanation session on the RCI report.
This will be followed by a question-and-debate session by the members of Parliament (MPs).
The debate session is then expected to be wrapped up by Zulkifli and Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Last Wednesday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul agreed that the
special parliamentary session
s on Tuesday would be held without breaks to provide sufficient time for MPs to discuss the TH RCI Report.
Fahmi said that at least 35 to 40 MPs have expressed their willingness to participate in the debate.
The 211-page RCI report on TH published on July 29 revealed various findings regarding the management and operational weaknesses of the institution during the period from 2014 to 2020.
Among the main findings of the RCI were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and profit distribution without considering the impact of depreciation and the decline in the fair value of investments.
According to the report, TH should have recorded
a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017
, instead of a profit of RM3.4 billion as reported, if the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) were fully applied.
The findings indicate that TH's financial position at that time was at a critical level, with a deficit gap between assets and liabilities existing since 2014, as well as several issues related to investment depreciation.
The report also identified several factors contributing to TH's financial crisis, including high grant payments, creative accounting practices, the indecisiveness of the Auditor-General, the expansion of TH's vision as a pillar of the ummah's economy, and the increased burden of the Hajj Financial Assistance (Hafis).
The RCI report also found the existence of suspicious transactions and information concealment, and therefore recommended that a forensic audit be conducted, in addition to urging the authorities to take firm and immediate action on every police report and complaint regarding the management and operation issues of the institution during the period from 2014 to 2020.
On Saturday, the His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia decreed that the investigation into the
RCI Report on TH
should be carried out exhaustively.
His Majesty said that this step is important to ensure that every responsible party is subjected to appropriate action, in addition to ensuring that the same issue does not recur in the future.
Enforcement agencies have also stepped up action following the release of the RCI report on TH, with investigations now focusing on individuals linked to alleged management irregularities at the institution.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has since
detained several people
as part of its probe.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drought declared in 'almost three-quarters' of England: UK govt
Article:
LONDON: Some 71.3 per cent of England is in drought, the UK government said Monday, after the nation experienced its driest July on record, with a fifth heatwave and scant rain forecast for the week ahead.
Parks and fields that are usually green at this point in the year were parched and yellow, according to AFP photos, as river levels dwindled and farmers battling low crop yields warned of possible food shortages.
"Almost three-quarters of England is now in drought as conditions worsen following a dry start to August," the environment department said, as parts of the central Midlands and northeast England joined other areas of the country experiencing prolonged dry weather.
"All regions of the country are experiencing pressure on their water resources," the department said, with "nowhere" in the UK having a "normal" status.
The Department of Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) said most of England is experiencing a "flash drought", which develops quickly and is the result of very low rainfall and high temperatures.
It is the third drought Britain – usually known for its unpredictable wet weather – has experienced in five years. More than 50 percent of England was declared to be in drought at the end of July.
Britain was also facing its fifth heatwave of the 2026 summer that has seen multiple temperature records being broken.
As much of Europe braces for another heatwave and prolonged dry conditions, scientists warn climate change is making extreme weather events more intense and frequent.
England and Wales both experienced the driest July on records, the UK's Met Office weather agency announced earlier, with England recording just 10 percent of its usual longterm average rainfall.
"There are warnings of more dry weather and another heatwave on the way, with temperatures tipped to reach the mid-30s in some places," DEFRA said.
The government has imposed irrigation restrictions on farmers and introduced a hosepipe ban in some regions, with more than 27 million people living under water-use restrictions.
There are now 45 million people living in a drought area, according to official figures. The total population of the United Kingdom is estimated at 69.3 million.
"We know the hot and dry weather is taking a real toll on farming and there will be long-lasting impacts on our environment," said the Environment Agency's Tony Grayling, who heads the National Drought Group.

Title: Masked man sets woman on fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 62-year-old woman suffered first-degree burns after an unidentified man  doused her with petrol and set her alight as she was opening a four-digit gaming outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong on Sunday.
The victim, Gan Siew Teen, had just unlocked the premises at  7.30am when the masked man, who was believed to have acted alone, approached and splashed petrol over her.
He then took out a lighter, ignited it and threw it towards the victim before fleeing on foot.
Gan, who lives within walking distance of her workplace, was taken to hospital and is now warded in the intensive care unit at Kuala Lumpur Hospital.
She suffered burns on her face, neck, arms and body.
Kepong member of parliament  Lim Lip Eng's personal secretary, Dic Lai, who met Gan's children at his service centre yesterday, said the family remained in shock over the incident.
"Closed-circuit television camera footage and eyewitness accounts revealed that the man arrived on foot, carried out the attack and then calmly walked towards the back of the building.
"Workers from a nearby restaurant who witnessed the attack rushed to Gan's aid and helped put out the fire."
Lai said Gan contacted one of her five children while waiting for an ambulance to arrive.
He said Gan lived alone near her workplace and, based on information from her children, did not appear to have any known enemies or debt-related problems.
"The family is also in the dark about what could have motivated the attack. They are devastated and still trying to come to terms with what happened."
Lim has offered a RM5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of the person responsible for the attack.
"Pouring fuel on a woman and setting her on fire is cruel.
"The person responsible must be arrested and made to face the full force of the law," he posted on social media yesterday.
Sentul acting district police chief Superintendent Jasni Zolpa said investigators were reviewing CCTV footage from around Taman Pusat Kepong to trace the suspect's movements before and after the attack.
"We have collected CCTV footage and are reviewing it. The identity of the suspect and motive for the attack are still subject to further investigation."
Jasni said the victim was in critical but stable condition.  It is learnt that the victim has been placed in an induced coma  pending surgery.
"The case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code."
Jasni urged anyone with information to contact Inspector Muhammad Amri Firdaus Jusoh at 010-9198209, the Sentul district police headquarters at 03-40482222 or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Colombia in state of emergency as quake kills 111
Article:
PEREIRA, Colombia: Colombia declared a state of emergency on Monday after a powerful earthquake killed at least 111 people, damaged more than 1,500 buildings and left an unknown number of people buried under rubble.
The 7.4 magnitude quake shook several cities across Colombia's coffee-producing region and the Pacific coast, sending terrified residents racing into the street.
Dentist Julian Pena was at home in Quibdo when he felt "very, very strong" shaking just after 7.30am (1230 GMT).
"People were praying in the street. It was overwhelming," he told AFP. "I ran outside carrying nothing and found hundreds of people there."
"There are many buildings with gaps, with cracks. There are others that have completely collapsed."
Authorities launched a massive rescue operation across several cities and put hospitals on red alert.
Cali resident Andres Felipe Mejia was among those who volunteered for the rescue effort.
"They pulled out a man and a baby, but the wife is still in there," he said near a pancaked multistory building.
"We are trying to get everyone out alive."
"A lot of people have come, with supplies, with food, helping the firefighters, helping the people," he said.
Authorities warned the toll could rise as rescuers searched collapsed buildings across several cities.
In Manizales, an AFP journalist saw many damaged buildings, including the crumpled tower of the city's beloved neo-Gothic cathedral.
"A great many buildings" in the city sustained damage, said administrative worker Jaime Zuluaga, 50.
"Traffic is paralyzed and people don't want to go back to their homes for fear of an aftershock."
[[nid:1508463]]
President Abelardo de la Esperiella, sworn into the job just three days ago, declared a state of emergency and vowed that Colombia would "move forward together."
The quake was felt across Colombia, including the capital Bogota, where crowds of people rushed out into the street in their pajamas.
"The quake was very, very strong," said content creator Valeria Polo, 29, in the capital, where only minimal damage was recorded.
At a depth of 110 kilometers (68 miles), the quake was felt in neighboring Ecuador and Panama.
Experts at the US Geological Survey said the quake was likely caused by movement along a deep fault within the Nazca tectonic plate.
Six airports suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said.
All upcoming professional football matches have been postponed.
Messages of support came in from countries across the region and the world.
"All my strength and love to my homeland. Let's hold each other tight," said Colombian pop megastar Shakira.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the United States was "closely monitoring" the situation and "stands ready to support the people of Colombia."
European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen said the EU had mobilized Copernicus, a satellite service, to help with rescue operations.
Israel, Mexico, Ecuador and France also offered assistance.
Latin America is already reeling from two disastrous quakes that struck Venezuela in June, killing more than 6,000 people and causing widespread destruction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says will demand conflict compensation from Iran
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Monday he would seek conflict compensation from Iran as part of any peace negotiations, citing attacks and killings stretching back decades allegedly backed or perpetrated by Teheran.
Negotiations on ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz have stalled, and his new demands risk putting a quick agreement further out of reach.
Trump's announcement was a direct response to Iran's insistence that US payment of war reparations are a pre-condition to any resolution of the ongoing hostilities.
"I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran," he said, noting that his demand included not only damages arising from the current war, but also Iranian attacks on US targets going back more than two decades as well as payments to the families of Iranian protestors killed by authorities over the past 50 years.
In a later post, Trump also said that the Islamic republic should be responsible for deaths and damage it caused in Lebanon, Syria, Yemen and Gaza.
In what has become a regular pattern, Trump last week threatened to hit Iran "very hard", potentially with attacks against civilian infrastructure, only to pull back, hinting a peace deal was near.
Trump this weekend said he was "low-keying" his approach to the conflict, suggesting that he was prepared to let economic pressure mount in place of further military strikes.
Digital media outlet Axios said that the US president did not express any frustration with Iran's delaying an agreement to open the Strait of Hormuz in their interview with him published Sunday.
Teheran has demanded that the US first end its blockade of Iranian ports and lift sanctions on its oil industry.
As negotiations have floundered, the strait's blockage by Iran has sent fuel prices soaring and rattled the world economy, putting pressure on Trump ahead of midterm elections in November.
In his post, Trump referenced the bombing of the USS Cole in 2000, which he has previously said Iran was "probably involved" in.
On Monday he said his various demands for compensations would be put "firmly into any, and all, future negotiations" with Iran.

Title: 'Myanmar refugees Asean's responsibility'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE issue of Myanmar refugees is Asean's collective responsibility, with lasting stability in the country crucial to stemming the flow of people fleeing abroad, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said Putrajaya wanted the Asean five-point consensus to remain the bloc's primary mechanism for dealing with the issue.
"This is an issue Malaysia must manage under Asean. It must be addressed together.
"That is why Asean centrality on the Myanmar issue is important. It is a common issue," he said after opening the 59th Asean Day celebration at Wisma Putra yesterday.
"We want the Myanmar government to fulfil the aspirations of Asean leaders because the consensus was agreed to by everyone. This includes Myanmar's leadership at the time."
The consensus was agreed upon on April 24, 2021 to address the political crisis in Myanmar following a military coup. It calls for an immediate cessation of violence, dialogue among all parties, the appointment of an Asean special envoy to facilitate mediation, the provision of humanitarian assistance through the Asean Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management and a visit by the special envoy to meet all parties concerned.
Mohamad said any proposed changes to the consensus would have to be referred to Asean leaders for deliberation and  approval.
He said Asean foreign ministers were tasked by regional leaders during a recent retreat in Cebu, the Philippines, to assess the latest developments in Myanmar and recommend the next course of action.
He said the consensus was not difficult to implement if there was sufficient political will from Myanmar.
"If they want to do it, they can. The five points are not difficult — engage with the parties involved, stop violence against their own people and hold engagement with all sides in the conflict."
He said restoring security in Myanmar was essential not only to prevent further refugee outflow, but also to allow those who had fled to return safely.
On Malaysia's plan to repatriate 5,000 Myanmar refugees, Mohamad said Myanmar had expressed its readiness to receive them, including taking them home by ship.
"The issue is the safety of these 5,000 people. Will they be safe? What will happen to them? That must also be considered."
He said the proposal was being examined by the Home Ministry, while Wisma Putra would facilitate discussions between the two countries.
No timeframe had been fixed, he said, but the process should be carried out as soon as possible.
He said the 5,000 comprised refugees from various ethnic groups.
"If they are from Myanmar, they are Myanmar refugees. They are not only Rohingya.
"There are various ethnic groups in Myanmar, including the Chin and Karen," he added.

Title: Government revives 1,647 abandoned housing projects
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE government has rehabilitated 1,647 abandoned private housing projects, with a gross development value of around RM153 billion, since 2022, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
Nga said yesterday this was part of the government's mission to eliminate abandoned housing projects by 2030, a key target under the newly launched National Housing Policy 2026-2035.
The progress followed the establishment of the Special Task Force on Sick and Abandoned Private Housing Projects in December 2022 and, as of June, it had benefited nearly 192,912 housebuyers.
"We will continue to strengthen the housing reform agenda to achieve our target of zero abandoned projects by 2030."
Nga said "prevention is better than cure", with the government implementing digital and audit-based reforms to prevent projects from stalling.
These include the housing integrated management system, electronic sales and purchase agreements (e-SPAs) and scheduled audits of housing development accounts.
"We are moving towards e-SPAs, where you can sign for a house in Kelantan even if you are in New York."
He said the government was also studying an "option to purchase" (OTP) mechanism with a "sunset clause" under the proposed Real Property Development Bill.
"By the end of this year, I will introduce the OTP with a sunset clause," he said.
The clause provides developers and buyers with a legal exit before a formal SPA is signed.
With it, developers who determine that a project is unviable within a specified period could withdraw, while buyers would receive a full refund of their deposits plus bank interest.
Conversely, buyers who found a more suitable property within the same timeframe would be allowed to exit, subject to certain charges.
Nga said the mechanism was aimed at preventing developers from being forced to proceed with large-scale projects despite poor sales, which he identified as a key cause of stalled or abandoned developments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From 'Made in Malaysia' to 'Made by Malaysia'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
GEORGE TOWN: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping jobs and industries, making early talent development critical to Malaysia's economy, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said AI and other emerging technologies are changing how businesses operate, requiring Malaysia to equip young people with skills to stay relevant in a fast-evolving economy.
Citing the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025, Akmal said 170 million new jobs could be created globally by 2030, while 92 million jobs may be displaced.
He said 86 per cent of employers expect AI and data technologies to transform their operations.
He said Malaysia must strengthen its talent pipeline to support the shift towards high-growth, high-value industries, especially semiconductors.
He said Penang is well placed to pilot an integrated science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) talent model, given its strong electrical, electronics and semiconductor eco-system.
Penang recorded 7.3 per cent growth in 2025, above the national rate of 5.2 per cent, with manufacturing expanding by 10 per cent.
The state's gross domestic product reached RM130.3 billion and accounted for 48.9 per cent of Malaysia's exports as of June, he said.
He said the strong industrial base has created high-value jobs, but the challenge is ensuring domestic talent can fill them.
"Industry and opportunities are already here.
The question is whether our students are ready to seize them.
He said Malaysia needs to prepare 60,000 engineers to move further up the semiconductor value chain, including strengthening capabilities from back-end to front-end activities.
He said the country must move beyond hosting factories and develop talent capable of creating higher-value products and technologies.
"We want to shift from 'Made in Malaysia' to 'Made by Malaysia'. It is not just about factories, but about our talent creating value."
He said STEM development must start early in schools and be strengthened through higher education, technical and vocational education and training, and industry training.
The ministry will allocate RM12.3 million over four years for Penang's STEM plan, targeting 100,000 students by 2030.
Akmal said the programme would link schools, industry and students and could be expanded to other states if successful.
He said companies should expose students to new technologies through workplace visits and school outreach.
"We want them to shape our future and lead in technology."
He said Malaysia's long-term competitiveness depends on talent that can drive innovation and strengthen its role in the global semiconductor supply chain.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Burnham vows to end 'subscription traps'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
PRIME Minister Andy Burnham has vowed to crack down on hard-to-cancel subscriptions and fake discounts as part of measures to tackle the cost-of-living crisis, said Downing Street on Sunday.
The announcement came as the new Labour leader was set to return to work after a vacation and begin a tour of the country to talk to people about their financial pressures, said his office.
Burnham said "people are sick and tired of rip-off discounts and subscription traps", where subscriptions are hard to cancel or automatically renew at a higher cost.
He said his government would be "making it as easy to leave a subscription as it is to join".
British consumers are "spending an estimated £1.6 billion a year on (subscriptions) they don't actually want", said Downing Street.
New rules would come into force in January next year, it said, forcing businesses to give customers "clearer up-front information, regular reminders and a much easier exit to contracts".
There would also be a new 14-day cooling-off period to let consumers cancel after a trial or renewal of a long-term contract, the government announced, without describing how this would be implemented.
Burnham also promised to tackle "misleading claims to customers about discounts" based on inflated full-price figures.
After nearly a decade as a regional mayor in northern England, Burnham has stressed his desire to move politics outside Westminster.
'The Mirror' newspaper reported his "cost of living tour" this month would cover all the United Kingdom's constituent regions and include places such as Port Talbot in Wales, an economically depressed former steelworking town.
"I'll be asking one question: what would actually make your life better?", Burnham told the left-wing newspaper.
Entering office, the prime minister promised to draw up a 10-year plan for the country.
His first announcements included a tax cut on energy bills inflated by the United States-Iran war, a cap on bus ticket prices and cutting business rates for pubs.
Opposition politicians on the right and left have criticised the measures as not going far enough.
—AFP

Title: Days of heavy rain leave at least 16 dead in Philippines
Article:
MANILA: Floods, landslides and accidents driven by a nine-day downpour equivalent to more than a month's worth of rain in some areas have killed at least 16 people in the northern Philippines, rescuers said Monday.
The rains, exacerbated by tropical storms, have led to school and government office closures across the main island of Luzon and flooding in the streets of the capital Manila.
Seven of the deaths occurred in the resort of Baguio, as a rain-drenched mountainside collapsed on three houses, city rescuer Esther Banawe told AFP.
Three people remain unaccounted for.
"Rescue efforts are continuing, but they are doing it manually because of the heavy rain," she said, adding that work was being supervised by a designated safety officer for fear of further landslides.
State weather forecaster Dan Villamil said rains in the vacation town, four hours north of the capital, were already 47 per cent higher than normal for the whole month.
"The rainfall recorded for August 1-9 was highest in Baguio, with an accumulated 1,413.2 millimetres (56 inches)," he said, adding the city's typical downpour for the month was 963.2 millimetres.
Parts of Metro Manila had recorded rain equivalent to about 90 per cent of a typical August, he added.
Landslides killed six other people elsewhere on Luzon, while another drowned, one was hit by a falling tree, and one was electrocuted, according to a civil defence office tally.
While heavy rain continued to fall Monday evening, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon told a news conference that floodwaters were receding.
"Our interventions are continuing, but we really need to fix the years and decades' worth of faulty flood mitigation interventions," Dizon told reporters, referencing a scandal over bogus flood-control projects that have cost taxpayers billions of dollars.
The Philippines is the first major landmass facing the Pacific cyclone belt, and the archipelago is hit by an average of 20 storms and typhoons each year, putting millions of people in disaster-prone areas in a state of constant poverty.
Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme weather more frequent, prolonged and intense.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US left-wing star reveals decision to freeze her eggs
Article:
WASHINGTON: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, one of the most prominent figures on the US left and a potential presidential contender, has revealed she is freezing her eggs, saying she wants to speak openly about choices confronting women balancing careers and family.
The 36-year-old Democratic congresswoman from New York shared videos of the fertility treatment on social media over the weekend, including footage of herself administering hormone injections.
"This is a choice that I am making to feel more in control of my life," Ocasio-Cortez said, describing her ability to undergo the procedure as a "very privileged position."
Her disclosure came as speculation mounts over her political future.
Hours later, Ocasio-Cortez said in a television interview that she had not ruled out running for the White House in 2028, while also leaving open the possibility of challenging Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer for his New York seat.
"I haven't ruled out the possibility," she told ABC on Sunday when asked about a presidential bid, while insisting her immediate focus remains November's midterm elections.
Ocasio-Cortez, widely known by her initials AOC, burst onto the national political scene with an upset congressional victory in 2018 and rapidly became a leading voice of the Democratic Party's left wing.
She said going public about freezing her eggs carried a "political risk," arguing women running for office face questions about marriage and children rarely asked of men.
"This is just not something that men deal with," she said. "Men run for office, or frankly they interview for jobs," without people wondering whether they intend to start a family.
Ocasio-Cortez also linked the decision to her advocacy for reproductive rights, saying political leaders should normalise conversations about women's health at a time when access to abortion and other reproductive care remains fiercely contested in the United States.
"In this political environment... I think it's important for us as leaders to have these conversations," she said.
Egg freezing involves stimulating the ovaries with hormone injections before mature eggs are surgically retrieved and preserved for possible future use through in vitro fertilisation.
The process can be expensive, is not always covered by insurance and offers no guarantee of a future pregnancy.
Ocasio-Cortez said she had been saving for the procedure and considering it for a long time.
She did not say whether she ultimately plans to have children.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Broadcasting DG Abdul Rahman Hamid dies at 73
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Broadcasting director-general Datuk Abdul Rahman Hamid has died due to a lung infection at Universiti Malaya Medical Centre (UMMC) yesterday.
He was 73.
His son, Mohamed Reza, when contacted yesterday, confirmed that Abdul Rahman died at 5.51pm after receiving treatment at the hospital for about a month.
He said his father had also spent two weeks in the intensive care unit (ICU).
"His remains are expected to be buried in Bandar Nusaputra, Puchong, tomorrow (today) morning," he said.
Abdul Rahman served as broadcasting director-general for six years, from 2003 to 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 107,000ha of forest, land affected by fires in Indonesia as haze fear grows
Article:
JAKARTA: More than 107,000ha of forest and land have been affected by fires across Indonesia as of Monday, with the government stepping up efforts to prevent transboundary haze from affecting neighbouring countries.
Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Djamari Chaniago said Indonesia had received no reports as of Monday that smoke from the fires was affecting other countries.
"We have emphasised to our personnel in the field that these efforts are not merely about extinguishing fires and protecting the environment and public health, but also about a national responsibility that we have," he told a press conference on Monday, which was made available through local media YouTube pages.
Djamari was responding to a question on whether the government was anticipating possible transboundary haze affecting Malaysia and Singapore and whether it had communicated with the two countries over the issue.
He said about 43 helicopters had been deployed for aerial operations, supported by between 10 and 15 fixed-wing aircraft, depending on operational needs, while substantial personnel and equipment had also been mobilised on the ground.
The minister added that weather modification remained among the most effective measures to tackle the fires, although operations depended on suitable rain-bearing clouds.
Forecasts indicated potential cloud formation on three or four days through Aug 18.
He said six provinces, namely Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan, were being closely monitored as the most critical areas.
He warned that strong El Nino conditions could accelerate forest and land fires and were expected to persist until around September or early October.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Major quake rocks Colombia and neighbours, at least 18 dead
Article:
BOGOTA: A powerful earthquake rocked Colombia and neighbouring Latin American countries on Monday, with at least 18 people confirmed dead in first reports as shocked residents surveyed destroyed buildings.
Emergency teams rushed to help victims and search for survivors in the rubble after geologists recorded the quake at a magnitude of 7.4 with an epicentre 100km deep in the west of the country.
The early-morning quake was also felt in Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela – itself hit by a devastating quake in late June – and prompted building evacuations in the Colombian capital Bogota, AFP reporters saw.
News footage showed collapsed buildings across western Colombia, though officials said they did not fear a tsunami.
At least 18 people were killed in the city of Pereira alone, Mayor Mauricio Salazar told Caracol Radio, adding "the situation is critical."
The governor of Colombia's Choco province wrote on X that there was serious damage in the provincial capital Quibdo, where video showed collapsed buildings.
Choco was at the epicentre of the quake, and the death toll from the area was not immediately known.
Alejandro Eder, the mayor of Cali, Colombia's third-largest city, reported at least 20 buildings had collapsed and people were trapped as "major damage" that was being evaluated with drones.
News outlets aired images of buildings also destroyed in cities such as Manizales.
'Strong, really strong' -
"There is no electricity or mobile phone coverage. It was strong, really strong. Things fell in my house," Martha Estrada, a 66-year-old resident of Eje Cafetero, which means coffee-growing region, told AFP.
"The quake was very, very strong," said Valeria Polo, a 29-year-old content creator in Bogota.
Six small airports in western Colombia suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said.
Bogota Mayor Carlos Galan said on Blu Radio that damage in the national capital appeared to be limited to cracks in the facades of houses and buildings.
President Abelardo de la Espriella announced he would travel to the quake-hit region.
In Bogota people ran out into the street in their pyjamas as emergency sirens rang out, AFP reporters saw.
Twin earthquakes in Venezuela of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 on June 24 killed more than 6,000 people and caused devastating property damage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Humble burrito causes indigestion for Trump's party
Article:
DEBATE  over the price of a burrito is causing indigestion for President Donald Trump's Republican Party, which fears being punished for the high cost of living in November's midterm elections.
The Mexican specialty — rice, beans, meat and other toppings wrapped in a tortilla — is beloved by many Americans as a comforting, filling and inexpensive meal.
Not any more, argues Andrew Kolvet, a spokesperson for the conservative youth organisation Turning Point USA (TPUSA).
"One of our TPUSA college students gave me his take on affordability: 'A burrito shouldn't cost US$20.'
"Yeah, a lot of this is a hangover from Covid and Biden-era inflation, but the lived experience is the same: It just feels like basic things cost too much," said Kolvet in a viral X post last week.
Those comments set off what Fox News, the Republicans' favourite channel, is describing as a "civil war" within the party.
Some conservatives questioned the cited price and accused American youth of having expensive tastes while others came to their defence — and warned of political fallout.
"Stop whining, get a job, eat ramen like the rest of us did in college, on a budget with four roommates.
"The market doesn't care what you think something 'should' cost," Dan Crenshaw, a Texas Republican congressman wrote on X.
In Washington, the price of a takeout burrito at two popular fast-food chains ranged between US$6.50 and US$13.50, depending on the ingredients.
Similarly, Marc Thiessen, a former adviser to president George W. Bush turned columnist, criticised students on the same platform for being lazy and paying higher prices for food delivery services.
"When I graduated I lived on ramen noodles," he wrote. "I didn't whine about affordability, I worked hard so I could one day afford a better life."
That prompted a sharp rebuke from Vice-President JD Vance, who called the comment surprising because "if you've ever met him in person, it's quite obvious the man has never missed a burrito", referring to the columnist's physique.
Other conservatives also said that comments downplaying consumers' concerns about prices was entirely the wrong response — and would have a political impact.
"If the Right's 'solution' to the affordability crisis is telling people to eat worse food, we will lose (in November), and we will deserve it," Angela Morabito, a spokesperson for the right-leaning Defense of Freedom Institute, wrote on X.
For his part, Trump again asserted on Thursday that inflation had decreased in the United States, denying any impact of his tariff policies on prices.
Inflation spiked to a three-year high of 4.2 per cent in May before falling back to 3.5 per cent in June as energy prices eased, according to federal figures.
Still, the murky outlook for the Iran war, which has caused gasoline prices to surge, has consumers worried.
A recent opinion poll from Marquette University showed that the cost of living was cited by 35 per cent of respondents as their primary concern, far ahead of the war in Iran.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Siti Kasim, another activist lose appeal over 2022 rally prohibition order
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today dismissed the appeals by activist Siti Zabedah Kasim, popularly known as Siti Kasim, and another individual challenging a prohibition order obtained by police to bar them from participating in a rally in 2022.
The rally was organised to demand the resignation of Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki.
In delivering the unanimous decision of the three-member bench, Judge Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli said the prohibition order was validly issued by a magistrate's court.
Sitting with Azhahari were Judges Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid and Datuk Ong Chee Kwan.
Azhahari said the order was issued when the rally was planned to take place during the National Recovery Plan, which was implemented during the Movement Control Order.
"The greater emphasis of the respondents at that time, in our view, was to ensure that Covid-19 pandemic could be put under control and the number of cases reduced," he said.
Azhahari also said the prohibition order did not violate Siti Kasim and S.Raveentheran's right to peaceful assembly.
"In fact the respondents did not stop the public from attending the said rally at the new venue at Bangsar MRT station.
"It was proven by way of affidavit evidence that the rally went on peacefully and the appellants also attended the rally albeit some delay," he said.
"In that sense, the appellants were not denied of their right to a peaceful assembly," he added.
Azhahari said the prohibition order did not violate Article 9 and Article 10 of the Federal Constitution.
The High Court had initially dismissed Siti Kasim and Raveentheran's application for leave to initiate the judicial review. However, in May 2023, the Court of Appeal allowed their appeal and ordered the case to be remitted to the High Court for a hearing on the merits.
On Sept 24, 2024, the High Court dismissed their judicial review, ruling that the magistrate's court order was part of an effort to curb the spread of Covid-19 at that time.
Siti Kasim and Raveentheran filed the judicial review application in January 2022, naming the then Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Noor Dellhan Yahaya, then Dang Wangi deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Muhammad Faizal Mohd Amir, the Inspector-General of Police and the government as respondents.
In the judicial review application, they sought general, aggravated or exemplary damages for the alleged violation of their fundamental rights to freedom of movement, speech and assembly.
Siti Kasim also sought compensation for having to endure embarrassment, experiencing stress and suffering severe leg cramps after being forced to walk from Lorong Medan Tuanku to a new rally location in Bangsar when police imposed a blockade at the original site.
At the Court of Appeal proceeding today, lawyer Kee Hui Yee appeared for Siti Kasim and Raveentheran, while Senior Federal Counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly and Federal Counsel Ng Wee Li represented the respondents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China is balancing Asia's crude  demand by itself
Article:
CHINA is singlehandedly doing the heavy lifting of cutting crude oil demand in Asia to compensate for reduced shipments from the Middle East as a result of the Iran war.
The world's biggest oil importer reported arrivals of 8.41 million barrels per day (bpd) in July, up from the near decade low of 7.12 million bpd in June but still 24.3 per cent below July last year.
If June and July imports are combined, it gives an average of 7.78 million bpd for the past two months. This is 4.21 million bpd below the average of 11.99 million bpd in the three months to the end of February.
The United States and Israel attacked Iran on Feb 28, with the conflict escalating to the point where the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed, cutting off a waterway through which about 20 per cent of the world's crude oil and refined products moved prior to the start of the war.
Two of the Middle East's crude exporters, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, have managed to boost shipments from ports outside the Strait of Hormuz, but flows from the region have still been knocked lower by around five million bpd.
The bulk of crude exports from the Middle East head to Asia, the top-importing region, which has seen crude arrivals drop substantially.
Asia's total oil imports in July were 22.82 million bpd, according to data compiled by commodity analysts Kpler.
While this was up from April's 18.77 million bpd, which was the lowest since November 2015, July's imports were still down about four million bpd from the average of 26.89 million bpd in the three months prior to the start of the Iran conflict.
What the data show is that the loss of imports by Asia is about equal to the drop in imports by China for the past two months.
Part of China's reduced imports will be because of price volatility, with benchmark Brent futures hitting a four-year high of US$126.41 a barrel on April 30, a time when June and July cargoes would have been arranged.
China has a track record of cutting back on imports when prices rise, but the scale of the drop has been unprecedented.
There is little doubt China has the ability to sustain lower imports for an extended period, given its vast crude stockpile, which is estimated by analysts to be at least 1.2 billion barrels strong and may even be substantially higher.
The question for the market is how long is China prepared to be the balancing force for crude oil in Asia?
China's imports are likely to stage something of a mild recovery in August, as cargoes that managed to exit the Strait of Hormuz during the brief ceasefire between the US and Iran are delivered.
China's imports from the Middle East are estimated by Kpler at 2.71 million bpd for August, up from 2.43 million bpd in July and the 1.42 million bpd in June, which was the lowest in Kpler records going back to 2013.
Total crude imports for August are estimated at 5.97 million bpd, but more cargoes are likely to be assessed as the month progresses, and it's likely that August imports will exceed those for July.
September imports are likely to be more revealing, as flows from the Middle East become more constrained given the return to sharply lower shipments through the Strait of Hormuz after the breakdown of the ceasefire deal between US President Donald Trump and Teheran.
Even if the latest moves to restore vessel movements through the strait prove successful, it will take several weeks for exports to ramp up and several more for those tankers to reach Chinese ports.
This means China's refiners can keep suppressing their appetite for imported crude and dip into inventories, or they can bid for cargoes from exporters outside the Middle East.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Growing threat of fake social media accounts
Article:
THE detection of more than 1,800 fake social media accounts, with many being used to stir up issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R) should concern every Malaysian.
Most of these accounts were on Facebook and TikTok, two very popular platforms in Malaysia. They often impersonate legitimate figures and organisations to publish false statements to trigger public backlash through gaslighting tactics.
The danger is not simply that they are fake accounts. It is that they can make manufactured sentiment look like genuine public opinion. This is particularly dangerous when 3R sentiments are involved.
Malaysia's fabric is complex, and sensitivities around race, religion and royalty can be exploited precisely because they provoke strong emotional reactions.
A false claim doesn't need to convince everyone, it needs only to inflame enough people to create distrust and division. There appears to be a pattern as well, if the past is any guide.
On March 3, Bernama quoted Communications Minister Datuk Seri  Fahmi Fadzil as saying that more than 10,000 fake accounts misusing the identities of the king and queen and other royals had been taken down since the beginning of the year. Yet, he said, there was no sign of it slowing down. One reason is certain: social media platforms are not quick in responding to Malaysia's request despite the Online Safety Act 2025.
The public is the last line of defence. Malaysians must resist the instinct to immediately believe, react and share.
A social media with thousands of followers is not necessarily authentic, while a post that appears to be going viral may have been deliberately engineered to appear so.
Let's not forget that when a million people repeat a lie, it is still a lie. Followers, likes and comments supporting the views have nothing to do with the content.
Cyberspace is inhabited by all kinds of people. And with artificial intelligence, it is hard to tell the fake content from the true one. But the public aren't without guidance. All they need to do is ask some simple questions. Who is behind the account? Is the claim supported by credible sources? Is the same information reported elsewhere, especially in mainstream media? Does the post appear designed to provoke outrage rather than inform?
Platforms and authorities must continue identifying and removing fake accounts, but enforcement alone can't solve the problem. Digital literacy and healthy scepticism are equally important.
The central message should be clear: before reacting to something designed to make us angry, Malaysians should consider whether someone is deliberately trying to make us angry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian boy feared drowned after falling into Subang Jaya river
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 7-year-old Indonesian boy is feared drowned after falling into a river at Persiaran Subang Indah, near a supermarket in Subang Jaya, tonight.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 8.06pm.
He said a team from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene, arriving 10 minutes later.
"Based on the initial report from the operations commander, the victim is believed to have fallen into the river at 6.30pm while playing with his friends," he said in a statement today.
He said the search and rescue operation was being hampered by the strong river current.
"The Water Rescue Team from the Shah Alam Fire and Rescue Station has also been called in to assist with the search operation," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three Malaysians arrested in Taiwan for acting as scam money mules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three Malaysians were arrested in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, last month for allegedly acting as money mules for a scam syndicate, reports said.
CNA yesterday reported that the trio, aged 18, 26 and 39, had entered Taiwan as tourists before being arrested separately.
According to the report, Zuoying police arrested the 18-year-old and 39-year-old suspects at separate locations while they were making cash withdrawals from automated teller machines (ATMs) at post offices.
The 39-year-old was arrested in front of a post office ATM, with police seizing NT$155,000 (RM19,660) in cash, two bank cards and a mobile phone.
The 18-year-old was also arrested in front of a post office ATM, with NT$60,000 (RM7,610) in cash, a bank card and a mobile phone seized from him.
The 26-year-old was arrested at Kaohsiung International Airport in the middle of last month following cooperation between Taiwan's National Immigration Agency and the Aviation Police Bureau.
Police seized NT$2,800 (RM355) in cash and two mobile phones from him.
The three Malaysians were among four foreigners arrested by Zuoying police in operations conducted between late June and July.
The Ciaotou district court subsequently ordered all four suspects to be detained pending investigations.
CNA quoted police as saying that scam syndicates were increasingly recruiting foreign nationals to enter Taiwan as tourists and act as money mules.
Most of the recruits were believed to stay in Taiwan for about a week before leaving the country after completing cash withdrawals on behalf of the syndicates.
Police believe the tactic is used to break the trail and make it more difficult for authorities to trace the suspects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 100ha forest fire in Sri Aman raises concerns over worsening haze
Article:
KUCHING: A fire has engulfed about 100ha of forest in Sri Aman, raising concerns that it could worsen the haze situation in Sarawak caused by transboundary smoke.
The fire broke out around noon today along Jalan Kejatau-Lingga, with firefighters managing to extinguish about 20ha of the affected area before operations were suspended about 7.50pm.
A Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department operations control centre spokesman said the department received an emergency call at 1.19pm, prompting a team from the Sri Aman Fire and Rescue Station to be dispatched to the scene.
"The seven-member team arrived at 1.35pm and immediately began firefighting operations using water from an open source at a nearby drain.
"Water was also supplied by tankers from the Rural Water Supply Department and the Betong Fire and Rescue Station to replenish the fire engines' water tanks.
"Firefighters also created firebreaks to prevent the flames from spreading further, with an excavator from the Sri Aman Department of Irrigation and Drainage assisting efforts to contain the blaze," the spokesman said.
He said firefighting operations would resume tomorrow due to darkness and limited water sources at the site.
The operation was also hampered by several challenges, including a lack of communication coverage, strong winds that caused the fire to spread rapidly, limited open water sources and narrow roads that made it difficult for fire engines to reach the affected areas.
Meanwhile, Sri Aman recorded an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index  reading of 114 as of 9pm today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Panic triggers 7-hour sea search for Bangladeshi labourer
Article:
KUANTAN: A Bangladeshi labourer sparked a seven-hour search-and-rescue operation after jumping into the sea during an Immigration Department inspection at a construction site in Tanjung Lumpur today.
The 25-year-old, who swam about 5km and hid in the nearby jungle for several hours, was eventually found safe at his workers' quarters at 5.30pm.
Search-and-rescue personnel were later stunned to learn that the man possessed a valid travel and work permit and had jumped into the sea after panicking at the sight of the large number of enforcement personnel at the site.
The operation, which began at 10am, involved more than 20 personnel from the Fire and Rescue Department, including its Underwater Rescue Team and drone unit, as well as police and the Civil Defence Force.
Taman Tas Fire and Rescue Department chief Mohd Hilmi Kashfi Mat Zali said the department received information from the Immigration Department at 9.35am about a foreigner who had allegedly drowned after jumping into the sea.
"Based on initial information from the Immigration team, firefighters conducted a surface search at the site where the man was last seen. The department's Underwater Rescue Team divers were also deployed to assist.
"Besides boats, the department deployed a drone during the search-and-rescue operation for the suspected drowning victim, while another team searched along the shoreline during low tide," he said.
Hilmi Kashfi said that at about 5.30pm, a construction supervisor informed the department that the missing man had returned safely to his workers' quarters in Tanjung Lumpur.
"Checks by the police revealed that the foreigner was the same person reported missing at sea earlier. He was handed over to the police for questioning," he said.
Hilmi Kashfi said the foreigner told search-and-rescue personnel that he had panicked upon seeing the enforcement personnel and jumped into the sea.
His supervisor later confirmed that the foreigner possessed a valid travel and work permit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid visits Ismail Sabri at IJN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today visited former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who is receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN) here.
In a post on X, Zahid also prayed for the Bera member of Parliament's recovery and continued good health.
"I pray that he will continue to be given strength and good health, that all his affairs will be eased, and that he will be granted a full recovery," he said.
Zahid also prayed that Ismail Sabri would be able to resume his service and daily activities as usual.
Ismail Sabri was reported to have experienced health problems while at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission on Aug 6 to have his statement recorded, before being rushed to IJN.
He subsequently underwent a procedure to implant a wireless pacemaker at the institute to treat an abnormal heart condition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK radio apologises after accidentally announcing King Charles' death
Article:
LONDON: A community radio station breached the rules after accidentally announcing the death of King Charles III in a May broadcast, a UK watchdog said on Monday.
Radio Caroline, a former pirate radio that now mostly plays rock music, apologised in May after airing messages falsely announcing the monarch's death.
One of the messages had said "we have suspended our normal programmes until further notice as a mark of respect following the passing of His Majesty King Charles III."
The national anthem was then played, followed by around 16 minutes of silence before the regular programme resumed.
The presenter apologised 30 minutes after the messages were initially triggered, Ofcom said.
The regulator, which received two complaints about the broadcast, said the "very significant inaccuracy" and the "considerable length of time" taken to acknowledge the error breached two of its rules.
One requires news reports to be accurate and impartial.
The other requires significant mistakes to be acknowledged and corrected on air promptly.
Radio Caroline told Ofcom the error occurred when a member of staff accessed sound files pre-recorded in the event of the monarch's death while carrying out maintenance on the studio computer, as the programme was being streamed remotely.
The staff member played the files "out of curiosity", which stopped the stream from the presenter's remote location and broadcast the files on air.
The person then reportedly "panicked and left the premises" after realising what had happened, according to the Ofcom statement.
Radio Caroline said the remote presenter "would not realise that they had gone 'off air' unless they were monitoring their output via an internet monitor."
The presenter, believing they were still on air, was not actively monitoring their phone and did not immediately respond to calls from people at the station who had noticed the error, the report said.
The station said the person who played the files had been "reprimanded" and had "apologised."
It added the pre-recorded files had now been removed from the studio computer. — AFP

Title: Another Malaysian arrested for drug smuggling abroad after pilot case in Indonesia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian was detained for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than four kilogrammes of hydroponic cannabis through Chennai International Airport in India.
Chennai Customs, in a statement published by India's Press Information Bureau yesterday, said the passenger arrived from Bangkok, Thailand on Aug 7.
It said the passenger attempted to leave through the Green Channel without making any declaration to customs authorities.
Chennai Customs' Air Intelligence Unit officers detained the passenger for inspection based on profiling. An X-ray scan of his checked-in luggage subsequently revealed suspicious images.
"Further checks found four packets containing greenish, lumpy substances emitting a strong odour, suspected to be high-grade hydroponic cannabis.
"The packets were concealed in a specially constructed compartment at the bottom of the checked-in luggage," it said.
Using a drug detection kit, Chennai Customs confirmed that the substance, weighing 4,033g, was cannabis.
The drugs were seized under Section 43(a) of India's Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985.
The suspect was subsequently detained and remanded pending further investigations.
"The public, particularly young people, are advised to be wary of sponsored overseas travel offers and opportunities to make easy money by carrying luggage of unknown contents when returning to India.
"Analysis of recent cases shows that drug trafficking syndicates often target young people by financing their travel, accommodation and other expenses before using them to carry and deliver prohibited goods to India," it said.
For the record, hydroponic cannabis is grown without soil using nutrient-rich water solutions, typically indoors under controlled lighting, temperature and humidity conditions.
The method allows the growth cycle to be managed more precisely and is often associated with the production of high-grade cannabis with higher tetrahydrocannabinol content.
In September last year, India's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence reported a sharp increase in attempts to smuggle hydroponic cannabis from Thailand through several airports in the country.
The agency seized 108.67kg of hydroponic cannabis suspected to have been smuggled from the country in several operations across India within less than 20 days.

Title: Hextar Retail draws 43 sen offer from major shareholder
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hextar Retail Bhd has received a conditional voluntary takeover offer from its largest shareholder, Hextar Portfolio Sdn Bhd, at a cash offer price of 43 sen apiece.
Hextar Portfolio, which holds a 30.6 per cent stake in Hextar Retail, is seeking to buy all remaining shares in the company that it and the ultimate offeror, Datuk Ong Choo Meng, do not already own, according to its Bursa Malaysia filing.
Hextar Retail currently has 464.99 million shares in issue, excluding 36.10 million treasury shares, of which Hextar Portfolio holds 142.29 million shares.
The 43 sen offer price represents a 7.5 per cent premium to Hextar Retail's last traded price of 40 sen on Aug 7.
It also represents premiums of 7.8 per cent, 7.4 per cent, 3.8 per cent and 0.3 per cent to the company's five-day, one-month, three-month and six-month volume-weighted average market prices respectively.
The offer is conditional upon Hextar Portfolio receiving valid acceptances that would result in it and Ong Choo Meng collectively holding more than 50 per cent of Hextar Retail's voting shares.
Hextar Portfolio said the offer price was the highest price paid by Ong Choo Meng and the person acting in concert with them during the three months before the offer period.
Ong Kook Liong, who holds three million Hextar Retail shares or a 0.6 per cent stake, is deemed to be acting in concert with Ong Choo Meng and Hextar Portfolio.
Hextar Portfolio and Ong Choo Meng intend to maintain Hextar Retail's listing on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia.
Shares of Hextar Retail closed at 40.5 sen, up half a sen or 1.25 per cent, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM202.94 million.
