Title: Simplified: The Tabung Haji RCI report and what it said
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Today, in a special sitting of Parliament, MPs are expected to debate a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the country’s Muslim pilgrims’ fund Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Here’s a quick and simplified summary on the 252-page RCI report and some of its key findings:
What is Lembaga Tabung Haji and what is its purpose?
It has two main functions: to administer or manage the fund (which includes the savings by depositors and investments); and to manage all matters regarding pilgrims’ welfare.
The Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) also enables TH to enter into joint ventures, buy and sell shares, and set up companies if approved by the Religious Affairs Minister.
How big is it?
Currently, TH manages the savings of over 9.8 million depositors.
Based on the latest statistics available on TH’s website, it was managing RM91.747 billion for 9.55 million depositors in 2024.
What is the RCI about?
The RCI was set up to:
investigate Lembaga Tabung Haji’s management and operation issues from 2014 to 2020;
determine if there had been any concealing of information and misleading statements given;
recommend appropriate action for any breaches of law.
When was the RCI conducted and when was its report released?
From its initiation to its completion and its release, the RCI spanned the administration of three prime ministers.
During Bersatu’s Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s time as prime minister, the Cabinet on August 14, 2020 decided there needed to be an RCI, and on July 14, 2021 agreed to set up the RCI and on October 8, 2021 decided on the RCI’s scope of investigations.
On January 20, 2022, the RCI chair, former chief justice Tun Md Raus Sharif and five other RCI members were appointed.
The report dated July 19, 2022 was presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on August 30, 2022, and this was when Umno’s Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was prime minister.
The Malaysian government declassified and released the RCI report on July 29 this year, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim explaining that it was not released three years ago as it could have caused depositors to panic and withdraw their savings from TH.
What did the RCI report find and what did it recommend?
1.Tabung Haji’s financial crisis in 2017; TH issued dividends (‘hibah’
) when liabilities exceeded assets
In 2017, TH faced a serious financial crisis as it actually had a RM1.4 billion net loss (instead of the RM3.4 billion net profit recorded in its 2017 financial statement), if accounting standards had been fully complied with.
The RCI said there were five factors that led to the crisis, including TH’s “creative accounting practices” in order to enable it to declare high dividends.
Under the Tabung Haji Act, TH can only declare dividends or distribute profits (hibah) if its assets are more than its liabilities.
But instead of waiting for the audited financial statements and using the asset values there for the years 2014 to 2017, TH used other methods (such as using estimated values via Realisable Asset Value; and tweaking when it should reduce asset values due to impairment losses) in order to have higher asset values for calculations on dividend rates.
The RCI said TH’s dividend or profit distribution (hibah) from 2014 to 2017 did not fulfill the Tabung Haji Act’s controls to ensure depositors are paid from actual profits and not from their own deposits, and the high dividends pre-2018 also caused TH’s reserves to shrink.
Among other things, the RCI said TH’s dividend or distributed profit in 2014 and 2015 exceeded its actual profits for the year, while its liabilities exceeded its assets in 2016 and 2017.
In 2018, the government had to bail out TH in order to close the deficit gap and enable TH to declare dividends for that year, and also to prevent triggering a “bank run” and market instability if TH failed to declare dividends.
This was done through the government’s fully-owned special purpose vehicle Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) using RM19.9 billion to buy over TH’s assets valued at RM9.7 billion.
TH could only pay 1.25 per cent dividend in 2018 when it started fully complying with the accounting standards, but has since been able to issue higher dividends — with the 3.5 per cent declared in 2025 being the highest in eight years.
2. Bonuses too high/unauthorised bonuses
The RCI said TH gave very high bonuses to its employees from 2010 to 2017 (including 2014 to 2017 when audited financial statements showed TH’s liabilities to be higher than its assets), and said this practice should be stopped.
The RCI notes TH had from 2018 started controlling bonus payouts, based on TH’s financial capabilities.
TH’s subsidiary TH Properties Sdn Bhd breached the Companies Act 2016 when giving unauthorised bonuses totalling RM1,148,400 to 14 persons (2017) and RM1.045 million to 10 persons (2018).
The RCI recommends getting back those unauthorised bonuses totalling more than RM2.19 million from TH Properties’ directors and officers.
3. How Tabung Haji’s governance can be improved
The RCI proposed multiple amendments to the Tabung Haji Act (Act 535) to improve TH’s administration.
This includes changing the law to specifically ban active politicians from being directors in TH and its subsidiaries, and to require TH directors to have specific expertise (such as in banking, accounting, economy) instead of only requiring them to be Malaysian Muslims.
4. Investments
Noting suspicious transactions and concealing of information, the RCI proposed a forensic audit on how problematic investment decisions involving 14 companies were made, which caused TH to face severe decline in asset values.
The RCI said TH and its subsidiaries’ directors, management and employees who were involved should be held responsible for these investment losses suffered.
The RCI said TH should focus on fund management portfolios, and should not be involved in high-risk investments (especially what TH classifies as “strategic investments”).
The RCI noted the expansion of TH’s original purposes to also being Muslims’ economic pillar had resulted in its investments in areas where it lacked expertise (such as properties and plantations), resulting in huge losses involving its subsidiaries.
The RCI proposed TH set up a new department (with the proposed name of Dana Haji or Haji fund) to manage investments and to be supervised by the Securities Commission of Malaysia.
5. Policy changes for deposits, pilgrimage payment, pilgrimage subsidies (HAFIS)
The Haj or pilgrimage cost per person has continued to increase from year to year, from just RM15,555 (2003) to RM22,900 (2019) and to RM25,540 (2022), with the RCI saying it is projected to go up to over RM35,000 (2030) and RM50,000 in 2050.
Currently, Malaysian pilgrims do not pay the full Haj cost, as TH has since 2001 been using its investment profits to subsidise up to half or more of the cost.
From 2009 to 2019, first-time pilgrims only had to pay RM9,980 even as the full Haj cost increased annually, while this was increased in 2022 to RM10,980 (paid by B40 pilgrims) and RM12,980 (non-B40 pilgrims).
The RCI said TH’s pilgrimage subsidy or HAFIS bill was projected to continue increasing amid rising costs, which would also affect TH’s profit distribution (hibah) or dividend issued to depositors.
So the RCI proposed TH change its policies:
Minimum deposit for depositors to be eligible for their turn for first Haj: To increase from RM1,300 to the current Haj cost paid by pilgrims (was RM12,980 in 2022) to encourage regular and disciplined savings;
To limit big withdrawals of deposits and require one-month notice before withdrawal;
Give Haj subsidies (HAFIS) only to those who need it; those who can afford should pay full Haj cost.
After the RCI report’s 2026 release, TH on July 30 said it has managed to keep Haj costs at RM33,000 per person for three consecutive years.
What did Tabung Haji say after the release of the RCI report?
Among other things, TH said it has already carried out 75 per cent of the RCI’s recommendations and is carrying out the others.
TH also said it had, since 2022, only announced dividends based on audited financial statements.
It also said TH is now in a stronger financial position and that it has started to rebuild its reserves.
TH said it has successfully tackled RM12.6 billion in investment losses via the 2018 recovery plan (RM10 billion through UJSB’s asset purchase) and RM2.6 billion in stages up to the end of 2025.
What happened after RCI report’s release?
Following the report’s release, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the police have launched investigations, while the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has also started investigating several individuals after finding discrepancies between their declared income and their assets.

Title: Decades on, Merdeka spirit still burns bright among older Malaysians
Article:
IPOH, Aug 10 — Do you still remember names such as Ali, Siti, Muthu, Jarjit Singh and Ah Meng that often appeared in our primary school textbooks once upon a time?
Those names, once so familiar to earlier generations, seem to bring back memories of friendship, unity and a spirit of togetherness in an independent nation.
That nostalgia was also felt by a group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, as this year’s National Month celebrations took them back to their childhood days and, although decades have passed, memories of celebrating Merdeka (Independence) remain fresh in their minds.
The waving of the Jalur Gemilang and the sound of patriotic songs once again evoked memories of Merdeka celebrations among the group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, bringing back the nostalgia etched in their memories.
With great enthusiasm, the senior citizens sang Merdeka-themed songs together, made Jalur Gemilang flags and took part in a flag-assembling game during activities held at the community centre, demonstrating that their love for the country has never faded with age.
For 60-year-old Bhajan Singh, from Gunung Rapat, the activities organised by the community centre are not merely a way to fill his free time, but also an opportunity to reminisce about celebrating National Day during his childhood.
He said the opportunity to get together with his friends from various races also rekindled the spirit of unity that forms the basis of the country’s harmony.
“Although I am getting older, my love for the country remains strong. My memories of celebrating the National Day for the first time are still fresh in my mind, although I was only a child at that time,” he told Bernama recently.
Seventy-five-year-old Jaharah Hashim, from Manong, Kuala Kangsar, said the activities at the centre gave senior citizens the opportunity to forge friendships while putting their minds to the test.
Older Malaysians from various ethnic backgrounds taking part in a batik-themed colouring activity at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak in Taman Lapangan Terbang recently. — Bernama pic
“In the past, we would simply wave the Jalur Gemilang, but now it is more enjoyable because we get to get together with so many friends. Although I am a senior citizen, my enthusiasm for celebrating the National Day has never faded,” she said.
For 64-year-old retired teacher P. Asokan, from Lahat here, the activities were truly meaningful as they brought together people from different ethnic backgrounds to appreciate the meaning of Merdeka.
“When I come here, I see Malays, Chinese and Indians all enthusiastically celebrating the National Day. This is the spirit that must continue to be nurtured so that we always appreciate the blessings of independence and national unity,” he said.
Meanwhile, programme coordinator Nur Hayatulasna Mohamed Fishal said the National Day-themed programme was held for the first time at the community centre as an effort to foster the spirit of patriotism among senior citizens.
She said various activities had been organised, including singing patriotic songs, making Jalur Gemilang flags with Pos Malaysia and a flag-assembling game.
“Although it was held on a small scale, we hope this programme can inspire the spirit of Merdeka among the participants and strengthen ties within the community.
“Their age is advancing, and their strength may have diminished, but their gratitude for the blessings of independence and love for the country remain unwavering, proving that patriotism knows no age,” she said.
‘Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’ (Malaysia Madani: Shared Prosperity), which has been selected as the theme for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM 2026) celebrations, among other things, emphasises that the country’s prosperity should be enjoyed fairly and comprehensively by everyone for the sake of shared harmony. — Bernama

Title: PKNS denies RM103.69m losses, RM6.1b debt claims as inaccurate and misleading
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 10 — The Selangor State Development Corporation (PKNS) today denied claims that it had incurred losses totalling RM103.69 million and accumulated debts of RM6.1 billion.
In a statement today, PKNS said allegations portraying the corporation as being in serious financial difficulty were inaccurate and misleading.
“It also does not reflect PKNS’ overall financial position.
“An independent assessment by RAM Ratings confirmed that PKNS remains in a strong and stable financial position. RAM Ratings continues to maintain its AA1/Stable/P1 rating on PKNS,” the corporation said.
PKNS said citing the loss and debt figures separately without explaining the corporation’s financing structure and overall financial position, created a misleading perception that did not reflect the actual facts and circumstances. — Bernama

Title: GPS ready for Sarawak polls regardless of redelineation outcome, says Abang Jo
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 10 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) is ready to face the state election with either the existing number of state seats or an increased number following the proposed redelineation exercise, its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said.
The number of seats to be contested would not be an issue, the Sarawak Premier stressed.
“We have no problem. If there are 82 seats, then 82 seats. If there are 99 seats, then 99 seats.
“We have no problem because it may not necessarily be 99 seats if there is insufficient time for its implementation,” he said at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Regency Specialist Hospital Kuching site here today.
He said the main priority was to ensure that the state election could proceed in accordance with the stipulated provisions and timeframe, without being dependent on the outcome of the redelineation exercise.
In July last year, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly passed the State Legislative Assembly (Composition of Membership) Bill 2025 to add 17 new seats, bringing the total number to 99.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported to have asked the Election Commission (EC) to prepare an updated report on the proposed redelineation exercise to increase the number of Sarawak state seats.
Madani Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the matter was raised at a recent Cabinet meeting, with the Prime Minister also expressing his commitment to implementing it.
The mandate of the Sarawak state government ends in February 2027. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji RCI report to face Parliament scrutiny tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10— Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan will present a ministerial briefing on the  Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020 during a special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow.
In a 35-second video distributed to the media, Zulkifli said he and Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan would also be involved in winding up the parliamentary debate on the report.
“The Cabinet has also indicated that action should be taken against those involved in the case,” he said.
The sitting, scheduled to begin at 10am, will allow MPs to scrutinise the 211-page report released publicly on July 29 after the government decided its findings should be disclosed.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil previously said at least 40 MPs had expressed interest in taking part in the debate. — Bernama

Title: Ewon, Donald retain Upko top posts
Article:
PENAMPANG, Aug 10 — Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Ewon Benedick has retained his position as president of the United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko), while Datuk Donald Peter Mojuntin remains deputy president after both posts went uncontested at the party’s 17th Triennial Delegates Conference at the Kadazandusun Cultural Association (KDCA) Hall here today.
Also elected unopposed were the five vice-presidents — Jairaiaz Joseph, Datuk Wong Thien Fook, Datuk Pangiran Lalung, Datuk Basari Sarikun and Datuk Dr Laurentius Nayan Ambu.
Meanwhile, several Upko party wings saw changes in leadership following their respective elections.
Carlye Lajimin was elected the new Upko Youth chief, with Newbaxter Tibin elected as deputy chief.
Carlye, who previously served as Upko central Youth deputy chief, replaces Felix Joseph Saang as head of the movement for the new term.
In the Upko Women’s Wing, Mohina Sidom retained her position as chief, while Lomiti Jahan was elected deputy chief.
In his winding-up speech, Ewon said he respected the democratic process and the decision made by delegates in the election.
He also congratulated all elected leaders, describing the outcome as an effort to further strengthen the party.
“This election should strengthen our party, not weaken it. All our party members are one big Upko family,” he said.
He also stressed the importance of making Upko an inclusive party by providing space and roles for members from different regions, divisions, religions and ethnic groups in Sabah.

Title: Kroll witness tells High Court she was unsure Jho Low was ‘number one’, confirms Najib received 1MDB funds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — An offshore asset recovery specialist testified in the High Court today that she could not confirm whether fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low, was the “number one” figure in the alleged conspiracy involving 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) funds.
Angela Barkhouse, managing director of Kroll (Cayman) Ltd and head of Kroll’s Offshore Practice, however, said that individuals who received funds would naturally be of interest to her investigation.
She was being cross-examined by Najib’s lead counsel, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, on the fifth day of the trial of 1MDB’s USD5.64 billion civil suit against Najib and six others, before Judicial Commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus.
Muhammad Shafee asked Barkhouse whether she had come across the name of fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, or Jho Low, during the course of her investigation, to which she answered yes.
He then asked whether she agreed that Jho Low was at the centre of the controversy and the alleged conspiracy to destroy 1MDB. Barkhouse replied: “Amongst others, yes.”
When Muhammad Shafee asked whether she would rank Jho Low as the “number one” figure in the alleged conspiracy, Barkhouse replied that she was not certain.
Shafee then pressed further, pointing out that there must have been other individuals or entities she had come across during her investigation.
In response, Barkhouse replied that those who received funds would be of interest to her.
Muhammad Shafee:
By that, you are implying that it includes my client (Najib). Is that correct?
Barkhouse answered, “That is correct”.
1MDB and its subsidiaries — 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited, 1MDB Energy Limited, 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited and Global Diversified Investment Company Limited, formerly known as 1MDB Global Investments Limited, filed the civil suit on May 7, 2021.
They named Najib; 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng; former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee; former chief investment officer Vincent Beng Huat Koh; former chief operating officer Radhi Mohamad; former investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jim; and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.
The writ of summons stated that the plaintiffs, among other things, accused the defendants of breach of trust, breach of statutory duty, abuse of power and conspiracy to misappropriate 1MDB funds.
The civil suit is being heard separately from the previous criminal proceedings against Najib.
On December 26, 2025, he was sentenced to 15 years in prison and fined RM11.4 billion for abuse of power and money laundering involving RM2.3 billion of 1MDB funds.
The trial resumes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Four Indonesian fishermen rescued after vessel sinks in Malaysian waters
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 10 — Four Indonesian fishermen crew members were rescued after their ship KM Samudra Jaya Kelautan sank in Malaysian waters while en route from Tarempa to Batam, Indonesia on August 2.
Pahang Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director First Admiral (Maritime) Mazlan Mat Rejab said that all the crew members, aged between 40 and 65, were rescued by a local fishing vessel (VNT) from Pahang that was passing through the incident area the day before yesterday.
He said the VNT then took all the victims to the Kuantan Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM) Jetty at around 5.30am on August 8.
“The ship was reported to have faced turbulent sea conditions and strong waves that caused engine damage before drifting for six days and eventually sinking in Malaysian waters while on its voyage from Tarempa to Batam,” he said in a statement today.
In the meantime, he said the Maritime Rescue Sub-Centre (MRSC) in Kuantan received information regarding the loss of the fishing vessel from Natuna BASARNAS on August 4, before the official information about the incident was received around 8.30pm on August 7.
Meanwhile, Mazlan said the four fishermen involved have been handed over to the Consulate of the Republic of Indonesia (KRI) today for further proceedings.
He said that his team also expressed appreciation to the local fishing community, especially the VNT crew, for their swift action and concern in helping to rescue all the Indonesian crew members. — Bernama

Title: HR Ministry: 541 Panasonic workers facing retrenchment to get govt help finding new jobs
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) is deploying early interventions to ensure that 541 employees of Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd who are facing retrenchment do not experience prolonged unemployment, through income protection assistance, job matching, and skills training.
Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said that the “from job loss to new job” approach is being implemented through collaboration between the Department of Labour Peninsular Malaysia (JTKSM) and the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) to ensure the welfare and career continuity of the employees are safeguarded.
“Kesuma will ensure that employees affected by job loss are given appropriate support and are not left to face this transition period without assistance. Through Perkeso, interventions will be mobilised as early as possible to help them obtain income protection and return to the job market,” he said in a statement today.
Ramanan said JTKSM, through the Subang Jaya Labour Office (PTK), received the Notification Form for Employee Retrenchment (PK Form) from the company on July 23 and 27, and conducted an investigation on July 27.
He stated that the investigation found a total of 541 employees, consisting of 415 local workers and 126 foreign workers, are involved in the retrenchment, which will be implemented in two stages on October 31, 2026, and March 31, 2027.
He said the company has committed to settling the payments entitled to the employees, including wages, wages in lieu of notice, payment in lieu of annual leave, and termination benefits, with an estimated total amount of RM64.38 million.
“As a follow-up action, Perkeso and JTKSM will hold further discussions with Panasonic tomorrow to coordinate actions regarding employee protection, benefit eligibility, and job placement interventions,” he said.
“Among the assistance to be provided includes advisory services and assistance for SIP [Employment Insurance System] benefit applications for eligible employees as temporary income support throughout the employment transition period,” he added.
Ramanan said Perkeso will initiate employee profiling to determine individual needs before providing assistance for benefit claims under the Employment Insurance System (SIP), career counseling, job matching through MYFutureJobs, and interview programs with employers who have vacancies.
Additionally, Ramanan stated that employees requiring skills adjustments will be offered reskilling and upskilling training programmes to enhance their chances of securing new employment.
Meanwhile, he noted that JTKSM will continue to monitor the implementation of the employee retrenchment and the payment of benefits in accordance with legal provisions, including taking enforcement action should the company fail to fulfill its responsibilities.
Panasonic Malaysia Sdn Bhd (Panasonic), had through a statement, announced the closure of production operations for two products, which will affect 400 employees by the end of March next year. — Bernama

Title: PKR congress to focus on reforms, economy and party strengthening, says veep Amirudin Shari
Article:
BANGI, Aug 10 — The 2026 PKR National Congress, to be held this week, will focus on the reform agenda, economic development and strengthening the party, said PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
The Selangor menteri besar said the importance of government stability and the party’s future would also be taken into consideration when making any decisions at the congress.
“So far, the motions are very clear. They concern politics, namely how to advance the reform agenda, develop the economy and strengthen the party, in addition to the president’s policy speech,” he told reporters after officiating the Human Ecology International Conference II (HEIC-II) 2026 here today.
On the party’s decision to grant Nurul Izzah Anwar temporary leave from her duties as PKR deputy president, Amirudin said it would not affect the proceedings of the congress.
“The party will certainly be affected to some extent, but we have a capable leadership team to shoulder the responsibilities, and the party has entrusted Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to carry out the duties of deputy president,” he said.
On August 6, the PKR Central Leadership Council (MPP) agreed to grant Nurul Izzah temporary leave from performing her duties as the party’s deputy president, effective after the 2026 PKR National Congress until further notice.
Asked whether Nurul Izzah’s decision had surprised the party, Amirudin, who is also PKR Election Director, said speculation about the matter had been circulating among political players for quite some time.
“I think the speculation had been around for a long time among political players, and I had also heard about it. It was only brought up now, and she also has to consider the timing, and we have to respect it... there is no point forcing her when there are several personal constraints that need to be addressed,” said the Gombak Member of Parliament.
Melaka will host the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh, for four days beginning this Thursday.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PKR president, is scheduled to officiate the congress on Saturday (August 15). — Bernama

Title: Police to file for inquest into deadly Durian Tunggal shooting this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Police will be filing an application for an inquest into the shooting incident in Durian Tunggal, Melaka, which claimed the lives of three people on November 24 last year.
The filing is expected to be completed by Wednesday or Thursday this week.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the inquest itself will take place in Melaka, although the exact date has yet to be determined.
He explained that the proceeding is likely to take considerable time, as all relevant parties will be called to testify, including the police officers involved in the shooting, who remain on duty but have been assigned to non-active roles.
On July 20, the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) decided that an inquest should be held to look into the matter.
The AGC stated that the purpose of the proceeding is to establish the cause and circumstances of the deaths, examine the facts surrounding the incident, and determine whether any criminal elements were involved.
On November 24 last year, three men aged between 24 and 29 were shot dead at an oil palm plantation in Durian Tunggal around 4am.
The incident is said to have occurred when one of the men allegedly swung a machete at a police corporal, leaving the officer in his early 30s with serious injuries to his left arm.
On May 26, Kumar reportedly said that the investigation paper was resubmitted to the AGC following compliance with several further directives sought by the prosecution. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu seeks more rangers to protect new Pulau Bidong state park
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — The Terengganu state government will submit an application to the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) for additional rangers following the gazettement of Pulau Bidong as a state park on July 16.
Terengganu State Tourism director Datuk Tengku Mohd Ariffin Tengku A. Rahman said the move was important to strengthen monitoring and ensure regular enforcement covering the land areas, islands and waters extending up to one nautical mile.
He said Terengganu currently has 511 rangers tasked with monitoring and protecting biodiversity across the state, including against encroachment and the illegal taking of forest resources and wildlife.
“Of the total, 330 are state-appointed enforcement assistants, while the remaining 181 are community rangers under Perhilitan and funded by the federal government.
“On July 16, Pulau Bidong was gazetted as a state park. So, we need additional rangers to protect the island from encroachment activities,” he said after the Terengganu-level World Ranger Day 2026 celebration at Wisma Darul Iman here today.
The event also saw the launch of the new Kenyir Rangers logo, symbolising the team’s renewed commitment to conservation and environmental protection.
Tengku Mohd Ariffin said the Kenyir Rangers had expanded to include 16 agencies, compared with 10 when it was established in 2017, with each agency having its own jurisdiction and responsibilities in the Tasik Kenyir area.
He said regular patrols and monitoring were conducted by the relevant agencies, with details of the operations not disclosed in advance to ensure effective enforcement.
“The operations are carried out by the respective agencies and are not publicised to ensure effective enforcement against activities that violate the law. During operations, teams are divided according to the respective agencies, with each operating within its own scope of responsibility.
“For example, the State Park Management Council’s jurisdiction is limited to the gazetted 32,000-hectare area, while the Forestry Department enforces laws under the National Forestry Act 1984.  Perhilitan, on the other hand, can enforce the law anywhere as it has no specific gazetted area. Where there are animals, there is Perhilitan,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Nine-year-old allegedly bullied at Kedah tahfiz school, father claims
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 10 — A couple have claimed that their nine-year-old son was bullied by a 15-year-old student at his school, leaving him with bruises on several parts of his body and face.
The victim’s father, Syamsul Azrin Man, 45, said he only discovered what had happened to his only child when he picked him up from a tahfiz school hostel here for a week-long holiday on July 30.
“I took my son home for a week-long holiday. At that time, I did not notice the bruises on his face. Later, when I noticed them, I asked him and he said he had fallen, but after I pressed him, he admitted that he had been punched by an older student the day before while wiping tables at the canteen.
“My son also told me that he had been kicked in the back, causing bruising. I immediately contacted a religious teacher at the tahfiz school, but the teacher told me that he did not know about the incident,” he told reporters here today.
Syamsul Azrin said he and his wife subsequently lodged a police report on the same day before taking their son to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital for further examination.
“The medical examination results showed that my son only suffered bruising, but what is upsetting is that he is traumatised and does not want to return to school because he is afraid of the older student who bullied him.
“Previously, I had noticed bruises on his body and a bump on his head, but my son said he had fallen. So, my wife and I left it at that, but he later told us that he had been punched, kicked and had his head pressed against the stairs by the same older student,” he said.
Syamsul Azrin said he and his wife were also dissatisfied with the school’s decision to dismiss their son following the incident, while the older student was only suspended.
Meanwhile, Kota Setar District Police Chief ACP Syed Basri Syed Ali said the case was being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code, and police had recorded a statement from the older student.
“We are waiting for the victim’s medical report from the doctor before any further action is taken,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PKR’s Wong Chen resigns Subang parliamentary seat, effective Aug 10, press conference Wednesday
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — PKR’s Wong Chen today confirmed his resignation as Subang MP, effective 5pm.
He said he had met Dewan Rakyat Speaker Johari Abdul on August 5 to hand over his resignation letter, allowing parliamentary officers three working days to prepare for the vacancy.
“We had a gentleman’s agreement not to release any details until August 10 at 5.00pm,” he said in the post.
“We shall also be removing the honorific title of Yang Berhormat from all our billboards, signages and correspondence by next month,” he added.
Wong also announced that he will hold a press conference on Wednesday at 11am.

Title: Housing Ministry resolves RM153b worth of sick or abandoned housing projects, says Nga Kor Ming
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) has resolved 1,647 “sick” and abandoned private housing projects worth RM153 billion, benefiting nearly 200,000 homebuyers to date, said its Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said the achievement was the result of efforts by the Special Task Force on Sick and Abandoned Private Housing Projects, established in January 2023 to address the issue and deliver a significant impact to the public.
Nga said the ministry is targeting zero abandoned housing projects by 2030 as part of the national housing sector reform agenda, supported by several mechanisms.
“These mechanisms include the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), Transforming and Empowering Data Usage in Housing (TEDUH), the electronic Sale and Purchase Agreement (e-SPA), periodic audits of the Housing Development Account (HDA), and the Option to Purchase (OTP), which will be introduced later this year,” he told reporters after launching the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035 here today.
Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and KPKT Secretary-General Datuk Dr M. Noor Azman Taib.
Nga explained that the OTP mechanism allows developers to withdraw from proceeding with a project within a specified period if sales are sluggish and the project is deemed likely to fail, with buyers receiving a full refund of their deposits.
At the same time, he said buyers would also be given the right to withdraw within a stipulated period, subject to the payment of administrative charges or interest to the developer.
He said the mechanism is expected to reduce the number of abandoned projects while safeguarding consumer interests and the sustainability of the national property industry.
Meanwhile, Nga said the government aimed to build one million affordable homes over 10 years under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), with the target based on actual housing needs and demand determined through big data analytics.
He said artificial intelligence (AI) technology would also be used to identify suitable locations, housing types and price ranges.
On home ownership, Nga said Malaysia’s home ownership rate currently stood at 77 per cent, compared with 42 per cent in Germany, 65 per cent in the United Kingdom and 66 per cent in the United States.
He said the government had allocated RM40 billion through the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) to assist first-time homebuyers purchasing properties priced up to RM500,000, including gig workers, entrepreneurs and small traders without fixed incomes.
To date, approximately RM18 billion remains available under the scheme, with 17 major financial institutions having agreed to serve as strategic partners.
Nga said about 95,000 individuals, including those from the B40 group, had benefited from the scheme. Eligible applicants are Malaysians aged 18 and above purchasing their first home valued at no more than RM500,000.
Earlier in his speech, Nga said the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035 reflected the Madani government's commitment to ensuring every citizen had access to quality and affordable housing that supported their well-being.
“Quality housing is not merely about providing shelter; it serves as the foundation for building prosperous families, harmonious communities and sustainable national development,” he said.
The DRN 2026-2035, themed “Humanising Housing”, shifts the focus of housing development from merely building houses to creating high-quality, safe, inclusive, sustainable and liveable communities aimed at enhancing the people’s well-being. — Bernama

Title: Over 600 emergency pumps ready nationwide as Malaysia braces for El Nino, says Irrigation Dept
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — A total of 606 portable emergency pumps of various specifications have been deployed nationwide and are ready to be mobilised as needed to address the El Nino phenomenon.
The Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) said the measure was part of its operational preparedness efforts on the ground when river or dam water levels fell to critical levels.
The portable pumps would be used to channel water supplies to agricultural areas, irrigation schemes and areas experiencing water supply disruptions, as well as to support forest and peatland fire-fighting operations with the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) and relevant agencies.
“The department also coordinates the integrated use of assets involving federal and state government assets and the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), while expanding technical assistance to Integrated Agricultural Development Areas (IADA) and other agencies according to current needs.
“Preventive maintenance programmes are carried out regularly to ensure all portable pumps and hydromechanical infrastructure remain in optimal condition before the drought begins. All requests for assistance are coordinated by the department, and the assets can be mobilised to affected locations within 24 hours,” it said.
In line with the national water sector’s digitalisation agenda, the department uses the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system and Pump Tracking System to monitor pump and water gate operations in real time, enabling disruptions or potential damage to be detected early and reducing the risk of water supply disruptions during the El Nino phenomenon.
Previously, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in its Long Range Weather Outlook updated on July 29, forecast that the El Nino phenomenon would continue until early 2027.
The situation is expected to result in lower rainfall in several areas along the west, east and southern coasts of Peninsular Malaysia, central and western Sarawak, and eastern Sabah, increasing the risk of drought and placing greater pressure on the country's water resources.
DID also said that it was monitoring 56 dams nationwide to ensure the effective integrated management of water resources, agricultural irrigation and flood mitigation, in line with the National Water Policy (DAN) and NADMA Directive No. 1 of 2024.
The monitoring covers dams under the supervision of DID, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS), the Sabah Water Department (JANS) and the State Water Regulatory Division (BKSA) through the InfoKemarau Portal and Reservoir Information Management System (RIMS).
“Water releases from dams are carried out in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure sufficient water supplies for domestic and agricultural use, as well as the safety of the dams. DID also works with state water supply operators to optimise the operation of water intake towers to ensure continuity of water supply to consumers,” it said.
In addition, DID has developed the National Water Balance Management System (NAWABS) as a national water balance management platform to help forecast drought risks and support early mitigation measures by providing projections of water resource availability up to two months ahead and early warnings up to 14 days in advance.
NAWABS currently operates in seven major river basins — Sungai Kedah, Sungai Muda, Sungai Bernam, Sungai Klang, Sungai Melaka, Sungai Kelantan and Sungai Similajau basins — and is expected to be expanded to 12 more river basins by 2028.
“NAWABS information is strengthened through the water resources assessment report prepared weekly by DID.
“The report contains information on river flow rates, dam storage levels and developments in drought conditions, which is shared with NADMA, the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), the National Water Services Commission (SPAN), DID top management and state offices,” it said.
The information serves as an important reference for determining mitigation measures, such as coordinating cloud seeding operations, issuing early drought warnings and planning water supply management in affected areas. — Bernama

Title: Any Melaka BN election deal must be made official, says state party chief
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 10 — Any political agreement involving Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election must be formally decided and should not be based on speculation or discussions on social media, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka BN chairman, said any negotiations on political cooperation should take into account various factors, including the strengths, weaknesses and advantages of each party before a decision is made.
He said parties interested in forming cooperation with BN for the state election were welcome to hold negotiations, but stressed that such talks would not necessarily result in an alliance.
“Negotiations do not necessarily have to end with the formation of a partnership. Many factors have to be considered before a person or party can become our partner.
“So I have always stressed that we should not draw conclusions from any unofficial discussions. This time, any agreement must be properly formalised and officially confirmed,” he told reporters at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.
Earlier, Ab Rauf officiated at the August 2026 monthly assembly of the state administration and the launch of the National Month and Jalur Gemilang Flag-Waving Campaign 2026 at the state level.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Umno chairman, said BN would defend the 21 seats it won in the previous state election, while the remaining seven seats could be open for negotiations, including the possibility of seat swaps.
The 15th Melaka state election in 2021 saw BN win 21 of the 28 seats, followed by Pakatan Harapan (PH) with five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) with two.
The mandate of the Melaka state government ends on December 31. — Bernama

Title: Melaka BN free to negotiate, Zahid confirms Ab Rauf empowered to lead coalition seat talks
Article:
GERIK, Aug 10 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) has been given the green light to hold discussions with any political coalition ahead of the upcoming Melaka state election.
As reported by
Harian Metro
(HM), BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he had empowered Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to lead the talks in search of common ground to ensure stable governance in the state.
“I hope the talks, which are usually complicated when it comes to seat allocations, can be handled amicably. There is no issue that cannot be resolved,” Zahid was quoted as saying.
He added that Ab Rauf, who also chairs Melaka BN and Umno state liaison body, would later present the outcome of the discussions to the coalition’s top leadership before any decision is finalised.
Meanwhile, Zahid, who is also Umno president, said he did not rule out attending PAS’s annual congress if he receives an official invitation, HM reported.
He added that if he is unable to attend personally, Umno would be represented by its leadership team.

Title: Three new housing laws planned as govt reviews Strata Management Act, says Nga Kor Ming
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) plans to draft and amend four housing laws under the National Housing Policy (DPN) 2026-2035.
The goal is to put in place a legal framework that is more thorough, forward-looking and equitable for all parties.
Minister Nga Kor Ming said the move involves three entirely new laws: the Property Development Act, the Building Managers Act, and the Rent Tenancy Act. In parallel, the government will also revise the existing Strata Management Act 2013.
Speaking to the press after launching the DPN 2026-2035 today, the Minister emphasised that under this new policy, the government is committed to finalising all four Acts as soon as possible.
Also present at the launch were chief secretary to the Government, Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar; attorney general, Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar; and KPKT secretary-general, Datuk Dr. M Noor Azman Taib.
The Minister also provided an update on the Property Development Act, saying it is already in the final stage of review.
He explained that this new law is necessary because the current regulations only cover housing projects, whereas the updated Act will broaden the scope to include commercial real estate as well, such as shop lots and other commercial developments.
Regarding the Building Managers Act, Nga said it is very much needed as Malaysia has nearly three million strata property units across more than 27,000 schemes, including condominiums and SOHO units.
With so many such properties, it is important to have proper rules to make sure they are well maintained, safe, and fit for living.
As for the Rent Tenancy Act, the Minister said this law is meant to create a fair balance between property owners and tenants. It aims to protect the rights and interests of both sides.
He also said the amendment to the Strata Management Act 2013 is necessary to keep up with the changing needs of managing strata properties.
This is important because urbanisation in the country has grown from 28 per cent in 1970 to 78 per cent to date, and is expected to reach 85 per cent by 2040.
Nga also shared that KPKT will roll out a big data analytics system starting next year to solve the problem of mismatched supply and demand in the housing market.
He explained that the system will combine data from state governments, local authorities, and KPKT, broken down by district and locality, as a reference for industry players.
“Our main problem is not supply or construction. The real issue is a mismatch. What is being offered is not what is actually needed, and that is why we have property overhang,” said Nga.
Developers can use the data system to carry out feasibility studies before starting any project. This way, the type, location, and price of the properties they offer will better match what the market actually wants.
He added that using the big data analytics system will not be mandatory for industry players. However, they can choose to subscribe to the system to help them make better decisions.
Nga also said that this approach will allow the definition of affordable housing to be set according to each locality, rather than using a single fixed figure for the whole country.
He pointed out that, based on National Property Information Centre (NAPIC) data, affordable housing in the Klang Valley is around RM500,000, while in Kelantan it is about RM300,000, due to varying income levels.
“As the saying goes, one size does not fit all. Imagine if the price of affordable housing in Kuala Krai, Kelantan, was the same as in Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur. That would not make sense at all,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Doctors confirm elective surgery success, PM Anwar Ibrahim under strict medical watch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has successfully undergone elective laparoscopic surgery to treat an abdominal para umbilical hernia, his medical team confirmed today.
The procedure was carried out smoothly under the care of specialist doctors.
Anwar is currently undergoing physiotherapy and remains under close observation, Datuk Dr Asri Ranga bin Abdullah Ramaiah, head of the Prime Minister’s medical team, confirmed.

Title: Pakistan PM wishes ‘brother’ Anwar swift recovery from medical procedure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wishes Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a speedy recovery from a medical procedure that the Malaysian leader is slated to undergo today.
He said the people of Pakistan joined him in praying for Anwar’s continued good health and well-being.
“Wishing my dear brother, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, a swift and smooth recovery during his medical procedures.
“May Allah SWT bless him with a speedy return to his duties,” he said in a post on X today.
Earlier, Anwar’s Senior Press Secretary Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said the prime minister was undergoing medical examinations and procedures prescribed by a team of medical specialists.
Anwar is expected to remain under observation for two days. — Bernama

Title: Refunds follow furore as Penang cancels 29,240 ANPR summonses, vows manual enforcement only
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) will cancel 29,240 summonses issued under the automated number plate recognition (ANPR) system between 2025 and August this year.
Penang local government and town and country planning committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the city council will also refund a total RM266,160 summons payments that was received in the same period.
“The ANPR summons system has been halted entirely so from now onwards, summons will only be issued manually by the enforcement officers,” he said at a press conference on the issue following public furore over limitations of the system.
He said the state government took into consideration the feedback and concerns raised by the public on the issue.
Among the issues raised were that vehicles which had stopped to drop off passengers were also issued summonses for illegal parking as the ANPR system could not detect if there were drivers and passengers in the vehicles.
“To ensure there are no disputes, all summons issued under the ANPR for illegal parking will be cancelled,” he said.
He said the ANPR system will now be reviewed and will no longer be used for enforcement.
“It will be used only to monitor but enforcement will be conducted manually after this,” he said.
He said those who had already paid the summons can submit their claims from both city councils for refunds by September 30.
As for those who were issued summons for not paying parking fees despite making payment within a 10-minute grace period, they can also submit an appeal for cancellation of the summons and a refund if they have already paid the summons.
They can submit their payment receipts and bank statement to level three in Komtar (MBPP) or email to perbendaharaan@mbpp.gov.my or to the enforcement directorate at MBSP, Level One, Pejabat Cawangan Jalan Betek, 14000 Bukit Mertajam or email to direktorat@mbsp.gov.my.

Title: Amirudin Shari: Pakatan open to working with Bersatu, Perikatan if stability maintained
Article:
BANGI, Aug 10 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) prioritises political stability and the people’s interests when considering any form of political cooperation with other parties or coalitions, said PH Presidential Council member Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
The PKR vice-president said PH remained open to establishing cooperation or reaching an understanding with any party or coalition that upheld these two principles.
“Cooperation with any party, not just Bersatu or Perikatan Nasional (PN), can be considered, provided the underlying principles remain political stability and the well-being of the people,” he said.
Speaking to reporters after officiating the Ecology International Conference II (HEIC-II) 2026 here today, the Selangor Menteri Besar also denied that Selangor PH had entered into any cooperation with Bersatu, stressing that no discussions or decisions involving the party had taken place.
Amirudin said any potential cooperation must be evaluated rationally at the central level, taking into consideration factors such as the timing of elections and other relevant circumstances.
“Of course, I cannot decide on my own, as I also share responsibility with the central leadership.
“So, if there are discussions (at the Selangor PH level), I will bring the matter to the central leadership. What exists currently are merely external ideas or views, which may stem from political realignments at the national level or in the context of a state election,” he said.
Last Friday, media reports indicated that Selangor PH appeared open to the possibility of collaborating with Bersatu, particularly at the state level.
The alignment is believed to be aimed at ensuring both parties remain relevant and strong ahead of upcoming elections, including the general election (GE) and the Melaka state election. — Bernama

Title: The death of plastic? E-wallets now displacing credit and debit cards across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Malaysia’s move away from cash has a clear winner. According to Ipsos Malaysia’s newly released E-Wallet Landscape 2026 report, e-wallets are only growing, but are supplanting debit and credit cards as Malaysians’ preferred non-cash payment method.
The numbers, drawn from a nationally representative Ipsos survey of 1,029 Malaysians aged 18-74 fielded in April 2026, tell a stark story of substitution over the past four years.
E-wallet usage among non-cash payment users climbed from 52 per cent in 2023 to 81 per cent in 2026 — a jump of nearly 30 percentage points.
Over the same period, debit card usage fell from 76 per cent to 56 per cent, and credit card usage nearly halved, from 15 per cent down to 9 per cent. Online banking and digital transfers held comparatively steady, moving from 70 per cent to 70 per cent.
As e-wallets rose, cards fell — while online banking, arguably a complementary rather than competing habit, stayed roughly flat.
Generational infrastructure shift
Ipsos frames this as more than incremental change. Overall non-cash payment adoption among Malaysians has climbed steadily too — from 51 per cent of the population in 2023 to 72 per cent in 2026 — meaning e-wallets are not simply taking share from a shrinking cashless pie; they are the primary engine expanding that pie in the first place, while simultaneously eating into cards’ share within it.
The report credits Bank Negara Malaysia’s push to strengthen the digital payment ecosystem, alongside the rollout of interoperable QR payment infrastructure (such as DuitNow QR, which lets a single QR code work across competing wallet apps), as key enablers.
That interoperability removes a major historical advantage cards held — universal acceptance — since a shopper no longer needs to worry whether a merchant accepts a specific wallet brand.
The displacement is most visible in everyday, in-person spending rather than online transactions. Ipsos data shows sharp usage growth for e-wallets at food and beverage outlets, tolls and parking, and retail stores — precisely the point-of-sale moments where a debit or credit card would traditionally have been tapped or swiped.
Bill payments (70 per cent) and money transfers (65 per cent) also rank among the top e-wallet use cases, encroaching further on territory once dominated by online banking and standing instructions tied to bank cards.
More competition
For banks and card issuers, the implications are significant: falling card usage can mean reduced interchange fee income and weaker card-linked product engagement, even as many wallets (like MAE) are themselves bank-owned, meaning some of this shift is a case of banks competing with their own card businesses rather than losing out entirely.
For everyday Malaysians, particularly those who have relied on a physical debit or credit card for decades, the practical takeaway is that acceptance and convenience have now tipped decisively toward wallets for routine spending — though cards likely retain an edge for larger purchases, credit-building, and online transactions requiring buyer protections that wallets don’t always offer.
Ipsos’s own assessment is unambiguous: Malaysia has moved “beyond digital payment adoption to digital payment dependence” — and for businesses and banks alike, sitting outside that ecosystem is no longer a viable option.

Title: High Court upholds blogger Jufazli Shi’s acquittal over YouTube post against Ismail Sabri, Umno
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The High Court here today upheld the acquittal of blogger Jufazli Shi Ahmad on two charges of posting offensive communications against former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and UMNO on YouTube and failing to provide police with the password to the account four years ago.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin upheld the Sessions Court’s decision after dismissing the prosecution’s appeal against Jufazli’s acquittal on October 18, 2024, at the end of the prosecution’s case.
“After reading the appeal record, the grounds of judgment of the Sessions Court judge and the submissions of both parties, this court dismisses the appellant’s appeal and upholds the decision of the Sessions Court judge to discharge and acquit the appellant,” Aslam said.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry appeared for the prosecution, while Jufazli was represented by lawyer Ramesh N.P. Chandran.
Jufazli was charged with creating and initiating the transmission of an offensive communication in the form of a video with intent to annoy another person through his ‘King Maker Politik’ account on YouTube at 3pm on June 27, 2022.
The link to the offensive video was accessed at 3pm at the Criminal Investigation Division office of the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters (IPD) on July 1, 2022.
The charge was framed under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and is punishable under Section 233(3) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment for up to one year, or both, upon conviction, and a further fine of RM1,000 for each day the offence continues after conviction.
Jufazli was also charged with failing to provide the password to his ‘King Maker Politik’ YouTube account, which was stored on his mobile phone, to a police officer at the Dang Wangi IPD at 12.10pm on July 5 the same year.
The charge was framed under Section 249 of the same Act, which carries a maximum fine of RM100,000 or imprisonment for up to two years, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Prevention is better than cure: Govt unveils OTP exit clause to stop sick housing projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The government aims to ensure Malaysia has no abandoned housing projects by 2030, with a new Option to Purchase (OTP) mechanism expected to give developers and buyers an earlier avenue to withdraw from projects that may no longer be viable.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the mechanism was part of a broader housing reform agenda aimed at preventing projects from becoming sick or abandoned in the first place.
“Prevention is better than cure. That is why I have implemented housing reforms so that our mission is to ensure that by 2030, Malaysia has no more abandoned projects,” Nga said at a separate press conference following the launch of the National Housing Policy 2026-2035.
Nga said the ministry’s special task force on private-sector sick and abandoned housing projects had resolved 1,647 such projects — as of today — involving RM153 billion and nearly 200,000 homebuyers over the past three years.
Among the reforms included in this policy are the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), the Transforming & Empowering Data Usage in Housing (Teduh) platform, electronic sales and purchase agreements, regular audits of Housing Development Accounts, a new Housing Development Act, as well as the introduction of an OTP and Sunset Clause.
Nga said the OTP mechanism was expected to be introduced by the end of this year.
He said the mechanism could provide both developers and buyers with an avenue to withdraw from a project within a specified period under agreed terms.
“For example, we give a period of six months. If within those six months the developer feels that the project is going to fail, the developer will have the right to offer an exit,” he said.
Under the proposed mechanism, deposits paid by buyers would be returned in full under such circumstances, together with the applicable terms set out in the agreement, he said.
Buyers could also exercise their right to withdraw during the specified period if they found a more suitable property, subject to charges and other terms under the agreement.
Nga said the mechanism was intended to allow both sides to reassess their position at an earlier stage instead of allowing an unviable project to progress until it became a larger problem.
“If there is no OTP, a developer may have to continue building. Once construction has started, even if sales are not there, they have to complete the project,” he said.
He said a developer could otherwise continue construction on a large project despite weak sales, eventually running into financial difficulties and leave buyers and the government to deal with the consequences.
Nga said HIMS, Teduh, regular HDA account audits and OTP formed part of a package of reforms being actively implemented by the ministry.
“I will monitor this every month to ensure that by 2030, our country has no more abandoned projects,” he said.
He said housing needs could be assessed according to individual districts and locations, including the number and types of homes required.
The system would also take into account local income levels and property prices, allowing housing supply and prices to better reflect conditions in different areas.
Nga said developers would eventually be able to subscribe to the system and use the information when planning projects, although its use would not be mandatory.
He stressed that all new housing projects would continue to be subject to requirements for developers to obtain advertising permits and developer licences.
“The government would not simply issue developer licences and would use available information to assess whether proposed projects were appropriate for the market,” he said, adding that the approach was intended to help create a more balanced property market while reducing the risk of future oversupply.
Nga also said the government needed to balance housing affordability with the need for property values to appreciate over time.
“Property ownership is not only wealth preservation. It is also wealth creation,” he said.
He said the government did not want house prices to spike, but neither should property values remain stagnant for decades.
“What we want is a gradual increase,” he said.
On housing affordability for the M40 group, Nga said lower home ownership rates could be influenced by various factors and should not automatically be attributed to affordability alone.
He said some people, particularly younger people and graduates, may prefer to rent rather than commit to long-term bank financing.
“We respect your choice and your option,” he said.
Nga said the government would therefore provide options for those who wanted to own homes while also developing a more structured rental market.
The National Housing Policy 2026-2035, launched today, proposes the enactment of a Residential Tenancy Act to create a more transparent, secure and balanced rental market.
Nga said the government’s approach was to provide housing choices according to people’s circumstances, whether they preferred to own or rent.
The policy also includes the phased implementation of the Build-Then-Sell (BTS) system to strengthen protection for homebuyers.

Title: Selangor govt to local councils: Don’t let land go idle, put it to use for urban farming
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 10 — Local authorities in Selangor have been urged to identify vacant plots of land to prevent them from falling into neglect or being occupied by unauthorised parties, including foreign nationals.
State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said applications could be made to lease the identified land for urban farming activities, including community gardens and programmes carried out by the private sector.
He said the move would enable vacant urban land to be managed more systematically while optimising its use for high-value agricultural activities.
“The state government has directed local government authorities (PBT) to identify idle land and apply for leases so that the sites can be utilised for community gardens, agricultural programmes or by interested private parties.
“This includes making the land available to PKPS (Selangor Agricultural Development Corporation) for agricultural programmes, ensuring that the land is used in a more organised and systematic manner,” he told the State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
Izham was responding to a supplementary question from Muhamad Izuan Ahmad Kasim (PH-Kota Damansara) on a proposal to use idle land for urban agriculture as a measure to prevent such areas from being occupied by foreign nationals.
He said the Petaling Jaya City Council was among the local authorities that had implemented the initiative in stages.
Meanwhile, Izham said the Urban Agriculture Programme (Community Gardens) continued to receive encouraging responses, with the number of projects increasing from 39 involving 390 participants in 2024 to 66 projects involving 990 participants in 2025.
He added that agricultural produce from the programme increased from 33.6 tonnes to 49.9 tonnes during the same period, while more than 200 community garden sites had been established within local authority areas.
He said the development not only encouraged greater community participation in urban agriculture but also helped increase food production at the community level and strengthen Selangor’s food security agenda. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak schools told to suspend outdoor activities if API exceeds 100
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 10 — All schools in Sarawak have been urged to continuously monitor Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in their respective areas amid the transboundary haze currently affecting the state.
The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said all educational institutions under its purview had been instructed to postpone all outdoor activities if the weather was too hot.
It said in areas where API readings exceeded 100, all outdoor activities involving students must be suspended.
“Educational institutions must stay updated on developments through the media regarding the haze situation in their respective areas or districts and comply with the recommendations of the Ministry of Health from time to time,” JPNS said in a statement today.
The department also advised students to wear face masks and drink adequate amounts of water frequently to regulate their body temperature.
“Schools should also ensure an adequate supply of clean drinking water and encourage students to bring their own drinking water.
“They should also remain vigilant and cooperate with nearby clinics and hospitals in the event of any complications involving students due to hot weather,” it said.
The number of areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy API readings due to transboundary haze rose to nine this morning.
Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas were Kuching (161), Samarahan (161), Serian (179), Sri Aman (155), Sarikei (155), Sibu (158), Mukah (156), Bintulu (142) and Samalaju (141).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.
API data is updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Five men remanded another week over murder of Batu Pahat businessman found in fishing net
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Aug 10 — Five men, who are being investigated in connection with the murder of a businessman here, have been remanded for another week.
Magistrate Aimi Nawwar Mohamad Othman granted the remand extension for all the suspects, aged between 26 and 40, at the Magistrate’s Court here today until Monday.
Their remand is to assist investigators who are probing the murder of a 39-year-old businessman whose bound body was found floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong in Parit Raja here last week.
The five suspects were previously in police custody and were remanded for seven days to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
Their initial remand application ended today.
On August 3, the body of the businessman was found floating along the river by members of the public.
The body was tied up and bound in a fishing net.
Initial investigations revealed that the victim was believed to have been killed by strangulation with a rope around his neck before both of his hands were tied with tape.
Police believe that the victim’s body was tied in a fishing net with five rocks before being thrown into the river.
Investigators believe that the rocks were used to submerge the deceased’s remains to prevent them from rising to the surface.
The victim was a businessman from Mutiara Rini in Iskandar Puteri and had been reported missing since July 29.
He was identified by his next of kin based on his clothing and personal belongings.
Of the five men arrested, two had prior records related to crime and narcotics.

Title: Terengganu MB says Jalur Gemilang flown without crescent moon and star was ‘unintentional’, ‘isolated’ incident
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the display of a Jalur Gemilang without its crescent and star at Dataran Batu Buruk was an isolated incident and was not deliberate.
Berita Harian
reported that he said the state government would investigate the matter after a video of the flag circulated on social media on Friday.
“I think this was not deliberate; it was an isolated and unintentional case,” he was quoted as saying.
Ahmad Samsuri said steps would also be taken to prevent a recurrence, regardless of whether the flag had been put up by the authorities or members of the public.
He was speaking after officiating the Terengganu-level World Ranger Day 2026 celebration at Wisma Darul Iman.
Kuala Terengganu mayor Lizan Che Mat, meanwhile, said the flag originally had the crescent and star, but the section bearing the symbols had come loose from its stitching following strong winds.
He said the Kuala Terengganu City Council (MBKT) removed the flag as soon as the issue was detected on Friday and replaced it with a new one.
He said MBKT would stop using stitched flags of that type and would instead buy fully finished flags to reduce the risk of a similar incident.
Lizan added that the council took the matter seriously and would ensure flags under its care were in good condition and complied with the required specifications.
